Mike had explained that he wasn't actually a resident here - as Xiao Zhang knew, he had been brought over by Shen Xing and Zhou Yan to investigate Zhou Wu's disappearance, so he didn't qualify for this welcome party!
But Manager Xiao Zhang had dragged him here anyway.
Unable to refuse, and seeing it as an opportunity to learn more about the apartment, Mike had come.
After Mike sat down,
Manager Xiao Zhang took out his phone to check the time and said to Jiang Ran, "Go outside and see if Wu You has arrived yet?"
Jiang Ran left the activity room and quickly returned.
He shook his head at Manager Xiao Zhang upon returning.
Manager Xiao Zhang smiled: "Seems he's either late or not coming at all! Tsk tsk, looks like he doesn't think much of this little manager!"
"Oh well, Jiang Ran, go get the things!"
Seeing Jiang Ran leave, a long-term resident suddenly spoke up: "Xiao Zhang, please don't tell me it's cake again this year?"
Manager Xiao Zhang waved his hand grandly: "No, we've got something new this time!"
The resident scoffed: "I remember you saying that before - calling it something new, but it was just changing chocolate cake to flower cake, then strawberry cake, and finally a mountain of cakes. I've eaten enough cake at these welcome parties to last a lifetime!"
Manager Xiao Zhang smiled without responding.
Soon, Jiang Ran appeared pushing a white food cart.
And with his arrival came the rich aroma of roasted meat.
Manager Xiao Zhang spread his arms wide: "This time we're having barbecue! And deep-fried skewers!"
The activity room fell silent for a moment before erupting in excitement.
Given the choice between preparing their own barbecue and having it ready-made, they clearly preferred the latter.
Accompanying the barbecue and skewers were ice-cold beer and soft drinks.
After Jiang Ran brought in the first cart of barbecue and skewers, he pushed in another cart loaded with chilled drinks.
"Jiang Ran, go join them."
Xiao Zhang told Jiang Ran to eat too, and Jiang Ran immediately found a seat and eagerly dug in.
Seeing everyone in the activity room focused on eating, Xiao Zhang suddenly announced: "Did you think that was all for this welcome party? Let me tell you, there's one more thing!"
Jiang Ran, who had been about to bite into a lamb skewer, froze at these words - there was more to this welcome party?
As the assistant manager, how come he didn't know about this?
Manager Xiao Zhang didn't keep them in suspense, announcing loudly: "Next up, please welcome... a clown performance!!!"
As he spoke, a person dressed as a clown entered from outside the activity room.
The person was about 1.8 meters tall,
with ridiculous clown makeup on his face.
The round red nose and exaggerated red lips were particularly striking.
Additionally, he wore an outrageous red curly wig and a red-and-white clown costume.
This clown entered differently from normal people - walking in with exaggerated crab-like steps, starting his performance the moment he entered.
"This is also one of our apartment residents, volunteering to perform for us at tonight's welcome party!"
"Let's sincerely thank him!"
"So! Everyone please enjoy the food and the show!"
After Manager Xiao Zhang finished speaking, he sat down beside Jiang Ran, joining him in eating barbecue while watching the clown's performance.
The clown immediately began performing in the open space at the front of the activity room. He performed with great energy - exaggerated movements and expressions, balloon tricks, juggling, magic acts, all quite impressive.
Meanwhile, in the live stream room:
Ultimate Rich Kid: [Does anyone know this performing clown's background? When I was little, my first reaction to clowns was that they were fun and funny. But now that I'm older and have seen so many clown movies, my first reaction is either violent criminal or horror. Which type is this clown?]ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
Fairy Sister: [That's a stupid question. People living in this apartment are either psychos or normal people. Which do you think he is?]
Ultimate Rich Kid: [I'm guessing normal, hahaha, just kidding.]
Fairy Sister: [...]
I am the Hero then said: [Rich Kid, I know this clown. And I've even seen him kill someone on live stream!!!]
Ultimate Rich Kid immediately became interested: [Now this is why I keep you around! Tell me more!]
I am the Hero: [This clown is a psychopathic serial killer. He loved clowns since childhood, and when he grew up, he became a clown performer, doing clown acts everywhere.]
[Because he particularly enjoyed performing as a clown, his hobby and profession complemented each other perfectly, creating a multiplier effect.]
[So he became a full-time clown, and as his performances improved, his income rose until he was making at least 30,000 yuan monthly - quite high for an ordinary person.]
[With his high skill level, he later took on several apprentices.]
[Eventually he started dating and married one of his female apprentices.]
[Unexpectedly, shortly after marriage, during a performance, the clown accidentally made a mistake that seriously injured his back. After a long recovery, he could no longer perform many difficult acts, causing his income to plummet.]
[The female apprentice couldn't take it. Shockingly, this apprentice was ruthless - instead of formally divorcing, she waited until the clown was away performing, then completely emptied their home after long planning.]
[When the clown returned from his performance, he was stunned to find their home completely bare - not even a chair left.]
[Moreover, the clown had always let his wife manage their finances, so after years of hard work, he ended up with nothing.]
Ultimate Rich Kid interrupted: [I get it, so he turned dark, right?]
[Becoming a psychopathic serial killer!!!!]
I am the Hero: [Wrong! Actually, this clown was quite psychologically resilient.]
[Even though his previous injury ruined his beloved clown career prospects, and he grieved for a long time.]
[And then his wife ran off with all their money, leaving him nothing.]
[But the clown pulled through.]

chapters.title: Chapter 102: The Clown’s Killing Obsession
chapters.content:
Although he had made it through, his heart was still riddled with countless wounds.
At this moment, you would never guess that he had gotten involved again with one of his former disciples!!!!
Ultimate Rich Kid: Damn, what a lucky guy! One or two female disciples falling for their master! If this was on those female-targeted platforms, it could be a whole novel!
I am the Hero: Wrong! You’re wrong again!
Ultimate Rich Kid, a little unconvinced: Where exactly am I wrong?!
I am the Hero: He got involved with a second disciple, but this second disciple is actually a guy!
Ultimate Rich Kid: ????? What the hell is this guy? Isn’t he a normal man? Even if he’s emotionally damaged, he should be with a woman, not a man!
I am the Hero: Actually, this clown didn’t even realize it himself at first. He’s bisexual and only discovered this after falling in love with the second disciple.
Ultimate Rich Kid: Are there really that many gays and bisexuals these days? First that refined old man in a suit, now this clown...
Domineering Female CEO popped up: There are actually many gays and bisexuals. Look at the emperors of the Han Dynasty in our country’s history—many had relationships like Longyang’s.Ultimate Rich Kid: …
I am the Hero: Alright, I’ll continue. After being with his male disciple, the clown had a brief period of happiness. But soon, the disciple grew tired of him and did something disgusting. At a same-sex gathering, the disciple drugged the clown and handed him over.
After that, you can guess what happened. The clown’s mind completely broke and twisted. He committed numerous murders, including that male disciple and the former female disciple, both among his victims.
If you search online now, you can still find some news about it. The Clown Serial Murders!
Ultimate Rich Kid: You’ve said so much, but you still haven’t talked about him killing live on stream!
I am the Hero: I watched him kill once. It was at the welcome party performance. After the show, he would go down and collect tips.
If there were viewers who didn’t tip, the clown would single them out.
If everyone tipped, then the one who tipped the least would be targeted.
Ultimate Rich Kid: Oh, so that’s the clown’s killing obsession or rule?
Damn, that means it’s a contest of who’s stingiest and who’s unlucky!
Interesting! This is only day one, and the welcome party at night already has hidden killing intent! The last round only had one death—boring! Wait, I just realized! If Jiang Ran and the other four lab rats don’t tip the least, and the stingiest are other perverted criminal residents of the apartment, will the clown still target them?
I am the Hero: Yes, the perverted criminals in the apartment are already hunting each other. The lab rats’ appearance just eased that tension.
Back to the Alice Apartment perspective.
At this moment, the clown had finished his performance.
After the show, like a magician, he pulled out a black top hat.
Wearing an adorable smile and exaggerated steps, he carried the black top hat and approached the crowd sitting below eating barbecue.
He began to collect tips.
The old residents below seemed to know the rules well. One by one, they took different bills from their pockets and dropped them into the black top hat.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
The more money given, the brighter the clown’s smile.
The clown came to the fitness coach, Sun Yijie, to ask for money.
To be honest, Sun Yijie didn’t want to give.
He thought from the start this was a free personal performance and never expected to have to pay!
Never mind that he had spent most of his funds being chased all the way here;
even if he had money, he wouldn’t want to pay.
He was used to freeloading. When he was a fitness coach, his female trainees didn’t cost him anything. So having to pay for anything voluntarily was more painful than death.
But seeing all the residents giving money, he couldn’t refuse—face was at stake.
He felt his pockets and found them empty, so he came up with a plan:
“Ah, sorry, I really want to tip, but I don’t have any change on me. Sorry about that! Haha!”
Sun Yijie thought that nowadays young people all use mobile payments. Who carries cash? So not having change was reasonable, right?
The clown said nothing. He placed the black top hat on the table and then put his hands in front of Sun Yijie.
Sun Yijie didn’t know what this guy was about to do. Was he going to slap him for not paying?
What happened next completely surprised him.
The clown suddenly clapped his hands together quickly in front of him.
The speed was so fast that because Sun Yijie’s face was close, the gust of the clap made him blink involuntarily.
When he opened his eyes again, he was shocked to see a palm-sized paper payment code appeared on each of the clown’s hands.
“Hehehe.”
The clown laughed at him.
Sun Yijie awkwardly pulled out his phone. Damn, this time he really had to pay.
He scanned the code and paid 10 yuan.
Then the clown continued collecting money.
He got to Mike next.
Mike was an American, and clown culture was very popular in the U.S.
As for this tipping request, Mike didn’t find it strange at all. After all, tipping was a common custom in white-majority countries like the U.S.
So he pulled out a 10-dollar bill.
Equivalent to 70 yuan in Chinese currency.
The clown kept collecting money and came to Wang Anjian. Wang Anjian was 22 years old, so he scanned and paid 22 yuan to the clown.
The collection continued nonstop.
Sun Yijie on the side watched with wide, envious eyes.
Making money this easily! If he ever stopped being a fitness coach, he’d become a clown actor collecting tips. Of course, that day would never come.
He cherished his various female trainees too much.
Finally, at the welcome party in the activity room, only two people hadn’t paid yet.
They were the manager Xiao Zhang and assistant manager Jiang Ran.
The clown came to them and first asked Xiao Zhang to pay.
After Xiao Zhang scanned and paid, it was Jiang Ran’s turn.
Jiang Ran naturally didn’t carry change, so he would have to scan with his phone too.
The question was: how much should he pay?
At that moment, manager Xiao Zhang quietly whispered in his ear:
“Just give 10 yuan as a courtesy. I gave 10 too.”
Jiang Ran nodded and then scanned the code to pay the clown.

chapters.title: Chapter 103: Psychopath vs Psychopath
chapters.content:
After collecting Jiang Ran's money, the clown turned and walked out without any intention of staying to eat barbecue or drink beer with them.
Back in the live stream room, viewers were watching as the clown exited the activity room through the main camera that continued tracking him.
The clown went to another activity room on the first floor after leaving. He turned on the light, closed the door, and sat on a chair near the table. Placing his black top hat containing various small bills on the white table, he took out his phone to check the payment records.
The organizers had clearly installed top-tier surveillance cameras throughout Alice Apartment. Viewers could clearly see the contents of the clown's phone screen through the live stream.
Seventeen people had scanned to pay. Fitness trainer Sun Yijie paid 10 yuan. Wang Anjian paid 22 yuan. Manager Xiao Zhang paid 50 yuan. Jiang Ran paid 10 yuan...
The clown now pulled out a small dagger from his costume pocket and made a light cut on his right index finger. The sharp blade easily drew blood that began flowing steadily. He started writing something on the white table with his bleeding finger while still looking at his phone.
Blood-formed characters appeared one by one:
Sun Yijie: 10
Jiang Ran: 10
Wang Tao: 10After putting down his phone, he pulled the black top hat closer and stared coldly at the loose change inside, as if trying to recall who had paid how much and identify those who paid the least. But after a moment, he pushed the hat away and refocused on the three names and numbers written in blood on the table.
I am the Hero commented: [The death list is out.]
Ultimate Rich Kid reacted with surprise: [These are the ones who paid the least tonight? Three at once? Will all three die?]Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
I am the Hero: [Last time there were two, and both died.]
Ultimate Rich Kid: [How brutal! But I'm shocked Jiang Ran is among them. After seeing him survive that headshot and counter-kill during the last live stream, I actually think this clown... might be in danger. The hunter could become the hunted when facing Jiang Ran...]
I am the Hero: [Hard to say. Last time the kite-making killer Wang Nuli didn't blow his head apart thoroughly enough. If he'd completely pulverized Jiang Ran's skull, could he still have survived?]
[Also this clown's killing methods aren't ordinary serial killer techniques. Personally I think his methods rank among the top I've seen in Alice Apartment.]
Ultimate Rich Kid expressed disbelief: [That strong? By the way, with three targets on the clown's list, who will he hunt first? Surely he can't hunt all three simultaneously?]
As soon as he finished typing, the live stream showed the clown taking action. After spacing out momentarily, the clown extended his left hand over the table and opened it, letting a dice drop onto the surface with a clatter - a standard six-sided die.
The dice tumbled across the table before finally coming to rest, showing six dots to Ultimate Rich Kid's eyes. Seeing this result, the clown moved his still-bleeding right index finger to circle Wang Tao's name.
Ultimate Rich Kid didn't understand this dice-rolling selection method: [Six sides for three people? How does this work?]
His real-life friend I am the Hero explained: [The names are written left to right - first Sun Yijie, second Jiang Ran, third Wang Tao.]
[My guess is numbers 1-3 correspond to each person respectively.]
[Similarly, 4=Sun Yijie, 5=Jiang Ran, 6=Wang Tao.]
Ultimate Rich Kid understood: [So Wang Tao dies first? When will the clown start hunting?]
I am the Hero: [Tonight. Last time he killed one per day.]
[With only two targets then, it took two days.]
Ultimate Rich Kid frowned: [I see. But who is this Wang Tao? Sun Yijie is part of this round's lab rats, Jiang Ran needs no introduction, but Wang Tao... I really don't know him...]
Fairy Sister chimed in: [His profile is available in the live stream room.]
[Wang Tao didn't appear in Round 26 but was in Round 25.]
In Round 25, Xiao Nuo lived in Room 904 while Wang Tao lived below in 804. When Xiao Nuo hosted loud parties with Xiao Peng and others, Wang Tao repeatedly came upstairs to complain about the noise.
After reviewing Wang Tao's profile, Ultimate Rich Kid commented: [This Wang Tao is quite ruthless too, but maybe from watching too many serial killer shows? He doesn't seem like your typical indiscriminate serial killer!]
[Aside from accidentally pushing a childhood friend into a river, his other killings all had personal motives - killing his college crush and her boyfriend after she chose someone else, killing his cheating wife along with their two children and her lover, then finally the noisy upstairs neighbors after multiple warnings.]
[These all had personal reasons! Seems if you don't provoke him, he's practically normal. Doesn't even seem like a serial killer.]
Domineering Female CEO nodded: [Compared to other psychopaths and serial killers, Wang Tao does seem relatively harmless.]
[But don't forget he's still killed over ten people.]
[It's just that his motives and patterns differ from typical serial killers, making him seem less dangerous.]
[But underestimate him at your peril. His current solution to annoyances is murder. Think about college - when the girl he liked chose another guy, normal people would just cry privately, but his abnormal response was murder. And he got away with it initially. So he's just a different type of serial killer.]
[Personally I think Wang Tao is still a developing serial killer, not yet fully matured.]
[Notice how with the noisy neighbors, he didn't immediately kill - first tried reasoning, complained to management, and only killed as last resort.]
[A mature serial killer would've killed at the first disturbance without discussion.]
Ultimate Rich Kid responded: [Really? Then I'm excited to see which of these two psychopaths survives! This is my first time seeing a direct confrontation between Alice Apartment's resident psychopaths!]

chapters.title: Chapter 104: Wu You and the Chainsaw Killer
chapters.content:
After finishing the barbecue feast, the time reached 8:30 PM as the welcome party concluded. People in the activity room began leaving one after another.
Manager Xiao Zhang stayed behind alone to clean up, telling Jiang Ran to clock out first.
Jiang Ran offered to help, but Manager Xiao Zhang refused, insisting he should leave first while he handled the cleanup slowly, along with finishing any leftover barbecue.
With no other choice, Jiang Ran left work first.
On his way back to his apartment 304, Jiang Ran unexpectedly encountered the American Mike in the same elevator.
He noticed Mike was heading to the rooftop.
"Going to the rooftop?"
Jiang Ran was puzzled. What would a foreigner be doing on the rooftop so late at night?
Mike smiled and replied, "I enjoy stargazing. I've set up a telescope there."
Jiang Ran suddenly understood. "Oh, stargazing! Hey, have you ever spotted any UFOs or aliens?" he asked curiously."Uh... well... not really," Mike answered.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
Jiang Ran said, "That makes sense. Most UFO sightings happen in America anyway. Maybe aliens prefer visiting there. That's why we don't see them in China."
This left Mike momentarily speechless, only able to respond with an awkward smile.
......
10:00 PM.
Wu You, who had spent the whole day caring for his father, came to relieve his mother who had just finished her night shift.
Though exhausted from tending to a cancer patient, Wu You knew his mother had it worse - working day shifts before coming to care for her husband at night.
What amazed him more was how his mother never complained, often comforting him that everything would pass.
Yes, everything would pass.
Wu You stepped out of his father's hospital room.
The hospital corridor at 10 PM was eerily quiet.
Pulling out his phone, he murmured, "Just two more hours until tomorrow when I'll get that ten thousand yuan."
Before signing the agreement to live at Alice Apartment, Wu You would have simply ridden a shared bike home after leaving the hospital.
But now he had to return to Alice Apartment - the middle-aged man had emphasized sleeping there nightly was mandatory to receive the payment.
He couldn't risk losing the money by not being there during these final two hours.
Grabbing a shared bike outside the hospital, Wu You took one last look at the darkness-shrouded medical building.
The thought of returning tomorrow to this money-devouring white hell filled him with thick dread.
Pedaling furiously, he raced toward Alice Apartment.
While taking the bus would have been ideal, the route stopped running after 9 PM.
Rideshares were too expensive, leaving the bike as his only option.
After a full hour of cycling, he finally reached Alice Apartment.
Parking the bike among the cluster of shared bikes outside, Wu You checked the time - 11 PM.
"Good, still within the timeframe," he smiled in relief.
Approaching the facial recognition entrance, he noticed lights still on in the security booth, shadows moving behind the illuminated windows.
This late-night sight of fellow awake souls comforted him, easing his sense of isolation.
Entering the complex, he headed toward the residential building, already imagining the luxurious bath awaiting him in his money-earning apartment.
A real bathtub! His room had one!
Having only experienced public bathhouses before, the prospect of his first proper soak lifted his spirits, his steps lightening with anticipation of both the tub and his impending payment.
The well-lit path from security booth to building passed uneventfully.
Arriving at the pitch-black lobby, he barely noticed the darkness - he was accustomed to it.
The automatic glass doors slid open.
When his foot stomp failed to activate expected voice-controlled lights, he pulled out his phone flashlight instead.
The beam revealed the lobby's simple, elegant decor.
Sweeping the light forward, he located the elevator - currently stopped on the 7th floor.
Pressing the call button, he waited while checking missed messages on WeChat.
Several @ mentions from the Alice Apartment residents' group caught his attention - all from Manager Xiao Zhang repeatedly asking if he'd attend the welcome party.
Private messages echoed the same inquiries.
Well...
Between caring for his father and catching a brief nap before his mother's arrival, he'd seen but ignored the notifications, deeming them unimportant.
"I've got no time for welcome parties," Wu You muttered. His father's care left no room for such frivolities.
Ding!
The elevator arrived.
As the doors parted with their cheerful chime, Wu You lowered his phone and moved to enter - then froze completely.
His body locked rigid, eyes widening in shock and terror.
Expecting an empty car, he instead faced a towering, broad-shouldered man wearing a grotesque mask and butcher-style attire - like something straight from a horror film.
Though unidentified, Wu You's body instinctively recoiled, stumbling backward away from this nightmare figure.

chapters.title: Chapter 105: The Price for Missing the Welcome Party Is Death
chapters.content:
The moment Wu You stumbled backward, the man inside the elevator pulled out a massive chainsaw from behind his back.
The man then started the chainsaw, its high-speed rotation producing a terrifying buzzing sound that chilled the soul.
If Wu You hadn't realized he needed to run now, he would have been truly foolish.
Though completely confused about the situation, he immediately turned and fled.
Being only 19 years old, his reflexes were far better than Zhou Wu's middle-aged father with deteriorating physical and mental capabilities from last time.
Wu You sprinted toward the automatic glass doors leading outside.
The towering chainsaw-wielding man chased after him with thunderous footsteps that echoed through the hall!
This chainsaw murderer was incredibly fast.
Within just a few strides, he caught up to Wu You and swung the chainsaw horizontally toward Wu You's neck. Fortunately, Wu You had been keeping an eye on his pursuer even while running. He quickly ducked and then straightened up, narrowly avoiding the deadly attack.
Next, he aimed for the automatic glass doors!Despite being exhausted from caring for his father all day, his mind remained exceptionally clear and quick.
He needed to reach the security booth - that would mean safety!!!
There were several security guards there!
Moving swiftly, he heard the sound of shattering glass behind him as he passed through the automatic doors - likely the chainsaw striking the glass.
This time, he didn't dare look back as before, fearing any hesitation would mean death.
So he kept running straight to the luxurious security booth at the main entrance.
The security booth's lights were still on.
Wu You grabbed the doorknob and found it unlocked. His heart leapt with hope as he pushed the door open while shouting:
"Call the police! There's a chainsaw-wielding maniac!"
But the joy on his face quickly turned to shock, then terror.
Because inside the security booth, there were no guards - only several human-shaped straw figures.
Wu You couldn't understand why rural scarecrows would be here.
But he realized now - those figures he'd seen in the security room when returning must have been these straw men.
"I'm done for... completely done for..."
No guards in the security room, and he'd wasted precious time here.
Cold sweat poured from his forehead.
Wu You turned to leave the booth and escape Alice Apartments, when excruciating pain exploded from his left side.
The unbearable agony instantly dropped him to the ground.
From a third-person perspective, one could see a young man screaming on the ground, his severed left arm lying nearby. Blood gushed from both the arm's stump and his left shoulder, as if calling to each other.
The chainsaw had taken his arm so suddenly that his mind and body hadn't immediately registered the pain, with adrenaline initially numbing the sensation.
But as seconds passed, horrific pain engulfed his entire being.
The physical agony was secondary to the soul-crushing terror and dread of approaching death that made his heart pound violently.
Wu You lay writhing, clutching his severed arm with his right hand while howling.
Tears and sweat blurred his vision, but through the haze, he saw the chainsaw murderer standing at the booth's entrance, both of them illuminated by the same light.
"You! Who are you?! Why are you trying to kill me?!"
Wu You had absolutely no idea why he was being hunted.
He hadn't made any enemies!
He was just an ordinary college student, one who'd taken extended leave to care for his sick father!
Who could possibly want him dead?!
The only recent change in his life was signing the agreement to live at Alice Apartments!
"Is... is this because of that?!"
Wu You's eyes became bloodshot, veins spiderwebbing across them.
He had seen the 10,000-per-day agreement as a lifeline.
Regardless of its authenticity.
So he hadn't questioned why such an incredibly generous offer existed.
Subconsciously, he'd assumed it might involve a haunted apartment or some reality show.
Never had he imagined encountering a chainsaw-wielding psychopath here!
Attacking him without reason!
If he'd known returning tonight would lead to this,
He would never have come back! Even if it meant losing that 10,000!
Now he regretted even more coming to Alice Apartments and signing that agreement.
Because without signing, none of this would be happening.
Even if he hadn't encountered the chainsaw killer tonight, it might have happened tomorrow night!
Ultimately, not signing would have been best - he'd never have faced this horror!
But in his current situation, he knew regret was useless.
All he wanted now was to know - who was this person?!
Why try to kill him?!
The chainsaw murderer only responded with a chilling chuckle.
Instead of removing his mask to reveal his identity, he pulled out a folded white paper from his pocket and unfolded it.
On the paper were printed words:
Why didn't you attend the welcome party?
The punishment for absence is death!
Seeing these words, Wu You's eyes widened in disbelief. His current nightmare was simply because he'd missed that welcome party?!
"You... you're Xiao Zhang?!"
In this apartment complex, having just arrived today, he only knew three people.
First was manager Xiao Zhang, second was assistant manager Jiang Ran, and third was Wang Anjian.
If the chainsaw killer was one of these three,
Wang Anjian was unlikely - they were both new residents.
That left Xiao Zhang and Jiang Ran as prime suspects.
Between these two, when Wu You missed the welcome party, Jiang Ran hadn't contacted him at all.
Only Xiao Zhang!!!!!
Had frantically tried reaching him!
The chainsaw murderer didn't answer, only continuing his eerie chuckle.
Then he raised the massive chainsaw and swung it down toward Wu You.
...
"FUCK!!!!"
At this very moment, on the rooftop of Alice Apartments.
Mike, the detective ranked tenth nationally in the U.S.,
Was watching everything that had just happened through his binoculars!!!!
After attending the welcome party, Mike had returned to his usual rooftop spot.
As in previous nights, he maintained vigilant observation of the entire property.
He hadn't expected anything unusual, assuming tonight would be as uneventful as before.
But to his complete shock, this had occurred!!!!
He'd witnessed the entire sequence.
He saw Wu You arrive by bicycle, enter through facial recognition, and go inside the apartment building.
Initially paying little attention, he was startled minutes later by Wu You's screams and immediately looked through his binoculars.
He saw Wu You inexplicably burst from the building with a chainsaw-wielding maniac in pursuit.
Then Wu You ran into the security booth, followed by the killer.
The booth's structure blocked his view of subsequent events.
At first, he thought Wu You might be saved.
But hearing the agonized screams from the booth, he knew - Wu You was doomed!!!!

chapters.title: Chapter 106: A Group of Black-Clad Figures on the Bus
chapters.content:
Mike was panting heavily.
To be honest, during his many years as a detective, he had certainly witnessed terrifying scenes of this level before!
However, those had all occurred overseas!
From his fluent and native-level Chinese, it was clear he had handled numerous cases in China.
But all his Chinese cases involved investigating affairs like divorce and infidelity, wealthy family feuds, or corporate espionage.
This missing persons investigation was his first in China.
Thus, he never could have imagined that investigating a disappearance would lead to such a scene!
A chainsaw murderer chasing people down?!
Especially happening right here!!!
He was certain this wasn't acting or a movie shoot.There were no directors or cameras visible nearby.
This was real.
A scene unfolding in the dead of night!!!
"I need to call the police! I have to report this immediately!"
After calming himself, Mike decided to call the police.
Let the local authorities handle this situation.
After making the call,
he continued observing the security booth through his telescope.
Only five minutes had passed since Wu You and the chainsaw murderer entered the booth.
Five minutes later, the chainsaw murderer emerged dragging Wu You by the foot with one hand while holding the chainsaw in the other.
Despite being on the tenth floor at night with poor visibility, his expensive telescope allowed Mike to clearly see Wu You's condition.
Wu You was undoubtedly dead - a horrific sight.
His left arm was severed. His abdomen was a mangled mess with intestines and organs spilling out, along with numerous chainsaw wounds covering his body.
This gruesome scene reminded Mike of five years ago.
He was now 33.
He had apprenticed at 15 and handled cases independently by 18.
From 18 to 28, nearly ten years, most of his cases involved various homicides, working with American police to capture killers for bounties.
During those years, he'd witnessed countless bloody scenes and confronted numerous serial killers and psychopaths - nothing unfamiliar.
But five years ago, at 28, something happened.
That incident made him avoid homicide cases entirely for these past five years.
Having not seen such gore for five years, witnessing it today in this completely unexpected way...
shocked him to his core.
Just from this brief observation, he could confirm that the person below, dressed exactly like the killer from The Texas Chainsaw Massacre,
was absolutely a psychopathic murderer!
Now, that chainsaw murderer was dragging Wu You's corpse into the apartment building.
A long trail of blood marked the path of the dragging.
Mike had no intention of going downstairs now.
He knew confronting the chainsaw murderer alone on the first floor...
would likely get him killed too.
So he decided to wait for the police.
However, instead of police, an entirely unexpected group of uninvited guests arrived.
Mike heard the roar of an engine.
Thinking it was police, he was surprised to see a black bus stop outside Alice Apartment.
Then, from both doors of the black bus, filed out numerous figures dressed entirely in black with black shoes.
Their faces were concealed by completely black round masks.
In the darkness, they'd be nearly impossible to spot if they wanted to hide.
After disembarking, they all entered Alice Apartment.
Some rushed into the security booth while others retrieved tools from the bus to clean the blood trail from Wu You's dragging. Another group entered the apartment building directly.
Even with Mike's extensive experience, he wondered if he was seeing things.
Were these sleep-deprivation hallucinations?
But after careful observation, he confirmed this was real.
This mysterious group was cleaning up and erasing the crime scene!!!!
Mike secretly photographed and recorded the scene below with his phone.
While waiting anxiously for the police.
The cleanup crew worked with alarming efficiency - clearly professionals.
In just ten minutes, all traces were gone. No evidence remained of the brutal chase that had just occurred.
Ten minutes later, they left.
Five minutes after their departure,
the police arrived.
Seeing the police, Mike who had planned to go downstairs, froze in place.
He remained on the rooftop.
Eyes fixed below.
Though he couldn't hear the conversations, he could see everything unfolding.
Mike could only watch silently.
Meanwhile, Far Neighbor game viewers still watching the livestream could observe everything like a movie or drama.
Below,
two officers exited their vehicle, approached the security booth, knocked on the window, and asked what had happened and who called.
Getting no response, they opened the window.ᴛhis ᴜpdated by NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
Finding it empty except for the light on.
Just as they grew puzzled, a figure ran out from the apartment building to the booth, opening the door to let them in.
The officers questioned the pajama-clad man about who had called.
This was Manager Xiao Zhang, who looked around confusedly and said no one had called!
The police called their station to check.
The call had come from an unregistered prepaid phone - untraceable.
Assuming it a prank,
they prepared to leave.
Before going, they asked if anything unusual had occurred, like chainsaw attacks.
After briefly checking outside and the first floor with nothing suspicious found, they drove off.
Livestream room.
11:40 PM.
Current viewers: 230,000.
Clearly many night owls were still watching.
Ultimate Rich Kid commented: [Hey, why didn't Mike go down when the police arrived?]
Fairy Sister replied: [If I were him, I wouldn't either.]
Ultimate Rich Kid: [Why not?]
Fairy Sister: [If those cleanup crews hadn't appeared, he definitely would have gone down. But after seeing them, no way. Being able to mobilize so many people to erase all traces so efficiently means whoever's behind this is dangerous. Revealing himself as the caller would be suicide. Mike's no fool.]

chapters.title: Chapter 107: The Clown Knocks
chapters.content:
No, Mike wasn't stupid enough to do something as foolish as going downstairs to turn himself in.
Although he had no idea his every move was actually being monitored.
From the information available to him, his actions made perfect sense.
Middle-aged Uncle: [Actually, if the cleanup crew had arrived faster, Mike wouldn't even have called the police. He thought the chainsaw murderer was just a lone individual, but that wasn't the case.]
Little Aunt: [Oh, there's no point discussing this. We should be feeling sorry for Wu You now! Wu You? Carefree... He didn't even last a full day, just a few dozen minutes short of getting that 10,000 yuan... With that money, at least he could have eased his father's medical expenses.]
Fairy Sister: [It's sad, but there's nothing we can do. Anyone who signs the agreement to enter the apartment is destined to die eventually, he just went earlier.]
[Of course, he was also more unlucky - he triggered the bad luck of not attending the welcome party.]
[There have been lab rats who died from not attending the welcome party before, though such cases are relatively rare!]
Ultimate Rich Kid: [By the way, is that chainsaw murderer really Manager Xiao Zhang?]
Although these livestream viewers could freely check any of the apartment's countless cameras,most people just followed the livestream's automatic main camera view. Who would bother manually checking other cameras?
Domineering Female CEO: [If you really want the answer, why don't you monitor Xiao Zhang specifically for a few days without missing a single second?]
At this moment,
due to Wu You's death, the long-haired beautiful host made an appearance.
"Lab Rat No. 3 Wu You has died. The total bets placed on him amounting to 1 million yuan have been transferred to the final prize pool."
Ultimate Rich Kid commented: [Speaking of which, what I admire most is this beautiful host. She seems to be available anytime, anywhere. It's almost midnight now, yet when a lab rat dies, she can still appear promptly to announce it.]
While everyone was still enthusiastically discussing,
the livestream's main camera quietly shifted to Wang Tao in room 804.
Now, at 11:50 PM, Wang Tao was still awake.
He was sitting in his living room watching a horror thriller movie,
completely engrossed in it.
During his time living at Alice Apartment,
he had watched numerous foreign horror thriller films.
The more he watched, the more a question nagged at him:
Many of these foreign horror films were based on real-life figures.
He had looked up their stories online himself.
After researching, he thought these people were truly deranged.
Although he himself had over a dozen lives on his hands,
all his victims had brought their deaths upon themselves through their conflicts with him.
But these killers often murdered complete strangers
simply because the victims fit their killing criteria.
Take the world-famous Jack the Ripper for example.
His victims were mostly impoverished prostitutes living in slums,
and his methods were extremely brutal - disemboweling, stabbing dozens of times.
Honestly, Wang Tao utterly despised such people.
He remembered when he was arrested,
crowds had called him a murderer.
But compared to Jack the Ripper and his ilk,
he considered himself practically benevolent.
In his short life, apart from accidentally pushing that childhood friend,
all his other victims had been people who'd wronged him.
At least he never harmed innocents.
"Jack the Ripper is just more famous. Honestly, I think he's overrated."
Wang Tao smirked disdainfully.
The reason he mentioned Jack the Ripper now was
because the movie he was watching was about him.
It was through films and novels that Jack the Ripper gained such notoriety.
Wang Tao felt that in terms of actual serial killer prowess,
Jack the Ripper's reputation far exceeded his real capabilities.
"Time for bed. I'll find another movie tomorrow."
Having finished the film, Wang Tao checked his phone - exactly midnight.
Rubbing his tired eyes, he turned off the TV with the remote,
then used his phone's flashlight to navigate back to his bedroom.
Yes, he always watched movies with the lights off -
it created better atmosphere.
Of course, while the ambiance improved,
so did the horror effect.
That was precisely the point.
Those with weak nerves definitely shouldn't try this at home.
Just a few meters from his bedroom,
in the silent night, he suddenly heard knocking at his door.
Knock. Knock. Knock.
The sound seemed to resonate directly with his heartbeat,
raising goosebumps all over his body.
Hearing the knocks, Wang Tao froze mid-step.
Who could be knocking at his door so late at night?
Wang Tao had two choices:
First, go to bed and pretend he didn't hear it.
Second, check who it was.
He chose option two.
Walking directly to the door,
he peered through the peephole to see his late-night visitor.
The hallway's motion-activated lights had turned on with the knocking,
allowing Wang Tao to clearly see through the peephole
that his midnight visitor was the clown from tonight's welcome party performance.
Yes, he had attended the welcome party tonight too -
staying home all the time got boring.
At the party, he'd even tipped the clown 10 yuan.
"So... did I not tip enough? Is that why you're knocking on my door in the middle of the night trying to scare me?"
Not knowing the clown's true nature, Wang Tao's comment was just casual banter.
"The clown..."
Wang Tao narrowed his eyes.
Having watched so many horror movies,
he knew there were countless films featuring clowns.
Traditionally, clowns represented comedy, jesters who brought joy.
But in horror films, they were pure nightmare fuel.
Wang Tao wasn't an ordinary person.
He was a highly educated white-collar professional
with over a dozen murders to his name.
Though he considered himself different from those deranged serial killers,
to regular people, he was just as monstrous.
For most people,
having just watched a horror movie
only to have a horror movie-style clown knock at their door at midnight -
no matter how brave they were, they'd shudder,
definitely wouldn't open the door,
and might even call the police if the knocking persisted.
But Wang Tao wasn't most people.
He opened the door without hesitation or preparation,
coming face-to-face with the clown.
"Hey, it's midnight," Wang Tao demanded directly.
"What are you doing knocking on my door in the middle of the night?"

chapters.title: Chapter 108: Wang Tao and the Clown's Deadly Game
chapters.content:
The clown giggled in a high-pitched voice that clearly belonged to a man, yet perfectly matched people's expectations of a clown's comical tone. "I want to play a game with you."
Wang Tao frowned. "A game? What kind of game do you want to play in the middle of the night? Shouldn't you be sleeping?"
The clown continued laughing in that exaggerated voice. "We'll sleep after playing. The game is... a deadly gamble."
When the words "deadly gamble" were spoken, Wang Tao's calm expression flickered slightly. He studied the clown before him and asked, "What do you mean by deadly gamble?"
The clown explained, "We bet with our lives. The loser dies, the winner lives."
Wang Tao thought for a moment. "What if it's a tie?"
The clown replied, "There can't be a tie. But if by chance it is, we both get to live."
Suddenly encountering a clown who wanted to play this kind of deadly game felt like something straight out of a horror movie. Most people would probably think they were dealing with a psychopath—someone who'd watched too many movies—and immediately slam the door shut.
But Wang Tao wasn't most people.
First, he took out his phone. "Wait a second, let me check something." He typed "clown murders" into his browser, which immediately brought up reports of clown-related killings and assaults from around the world. Finding what he needed, he held up his phone for the clown to see. "Is this you?"The clown nodded.
Wang Tao smiled and put away his phone. "Oh, so you're just like me—another transparent person caged here. Looks like if I don't play your game tonight, I won't be getting any sleep anyway. Fine then, let's do it."
With a wave, Wang Tao led the clown into his living room and closed the door behind them—a bold move indeed.
The two now sat facing each other across the glass coffee table in the living room. Wang Tao spoke first: "Why choose me for this game?"
The clown grinned. "Because you're one of the people who paid the least tonight."
Wang Tao blinked. "One of? So there are others?"
"Two more," the clown said.
"Have you already approached them? Or am I first?"
"You're the first."
"My luck's that bad, huh?" Wang Tao mused. "How exactly did you pick me as first? Because I seem easy to bully?"The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the NovᴇlFirenᴇt
The clown laughed. "I rolled dice to choose you."
"Ridiculous." Wang Tao shook his head. "Completely ridiculous. Though this is actually my first time meeting a serial killer in real life. When I got caught before, none of my prison buddies dared come near me."
After a pause, Wang Tao asked, "So how does this deadly gamble work?"
The clown suggested, "How about cards? Fifty-four cards, each draws one. Best two out of three, higher number wins."
Wang Tao immediately rejected this. "No cards. You're a clown—I saw your performance tonight. Your hands are way too fast. Any card game would be too easy for you to cheat at."
The clown seemed taken aback—probably the first time someone had refused his game. Most of his previous victims either panicked or tried to fight back immediately upon realizing the situation. Few remained calm enough to even sit down, let alone reject the proposed game as unfair.
Rather than getting angry, the clown burst into exaggerated laughter, clutching his stomach. Then with a dramatic clap of his hands, a cascade of cards appeared between his palms like magic before vanishing just as suddenly.
"If not cards," the clown proposed, "then dice? Roll for highest number, best two out of three?"
Wang Tao shook his head again. "Same problem as cards—too easy to cheat. Not fair to me."
Still unperturbed, the clown's painted smile stretched even wider. "Then you suggest a game."
After some thought, Wang Tao said, "Here's what we'll do: I'll take ten sticky notes, number them one through ten, crumple each into a ball, and put them in a box. We'll each draw one and compare numbers—best two out of three. Pure luck. That's what I call gambling with your life."
The clown considered this, then countered, "I accept, with one addition: include one hundred blank sticky notes crumpled up with the numbered ones. Blanks count as zero. If we both draw zeros, it's a tie. First to win two rounds takes all. Agreed?"
Wang Tao nodded after a moment's consideration and went to his bedroom to retrieve a pen and square sticky notes.
Meanwhile, in the live stream room:
Ultimate Rich Kid: [Thank goodness I spent the week after round 26 catching up on sleep and recovering, otherwise I'd be running on coffee right now.]
[The clown's finally making his move, though not exactly how I imagined. I thought he'd just kill outright, but instead he's playing games with Wang Tao.]
[Where's the martial arts expert? Did the clown follow this same routine with his last two victims?]
When Ultimate Rich Kid asked I am the Hero, there was no response.
Domineering Female CEO: [Your friend's probably asleep.]
[I'll tell you—the first lab rat didn't even play the game. Went completely hysterical and tried to fight back. Didn't help—still got killed.]
[The second one had better nerves and played cards with the clown. Lost and got drilled to death with a power drill.]
Ultimate Rich Kid: [I see... Hey, CEO, do you think the clown cheated during that card game with the lab rat?]
Domineering Female CEO: [No way to know for sure. Magicians' hands are too fast—you'd need an expert to spot it. But I suspect he did cheat—otherwise there's no way he could've won all three rounds in that best-two-out-of-three.]
Ultimate Rich Kid: [In that case, I'm finding fellow psycho Wang Tao much more interesting! He immediately ruled out cards and dice to avoid cheating, going straight for the blind draw.]
Domineering Female CEO: [True, but the paper ball blind draw isn't completely fair either—it can still be rigged. With just the ten numbered balls Wang Tao proposed, cheating wouldn't be too hard. Adding the clown's hundred blank zeros makes it more difficult though.]
Ultimate Rich Kid: [Wait, you can cheat at drawing paper balls? How? Even with just ten, I don't see how that's possible!]
Domineering Female CEO: [You're too naive. If they were identical hard plastic balls with numbers, sure—but crumpled paper balls have unique shapes. Someone could remember how they folded a particular number beforehand and identify it by touch.]
[Though with a hundred blanks added in, like I said, the difficulty increases significantly.]
[Of course, that's just one possible method—the actual cheating technique depends on the specific game situation.]

chapters.title: Chapter 109: Wang Tao Cheats, The Clown’s Unbelievable Luck
chapters.content:
At this moment, Wang Tao began writing the numbers 1 to 10 on ten separate sticky notes.
After finishing, Wang Tao handed them over to the clown for inspection.
Once the clown finished checking, Wang Tao crumpled the notes into balls right in front of him and tossed them into an opaque rectangular liquor box he had found.
After throwing in the ten numbered paper balls, Wang Tao and the clown each grabbed fifty more sticky notes, crumpled them into balls, and threw them into the rectangular liquor box.
While crumpling the paper balls, Wang Tao quietly observed the clown in front of him.
He realized this clown was very different from the clown performers he had seen before.
The clowns he had seen on stage would perform as clowns, and after the show, even if their clown makeup was still on their faces and they wore silly clown costumes, once offstage, they would immediately return to looking like normal people.
After all, those people were just professional clowns. Their profession was one thing, and their life another. They kept them well separated.
But this clown before him...
Whether it was the performance at the welcome party or now during everyday moments, he gave off the vibe of a genuinely ridiculous clown.“He’s just a clown, after all,” Wang Tao thought with disdain.
Right now, Wang Tao had an extremely strong desire to live.
He liked his current life. This was the most relaxed and comfortable stage of his life, so under no circumstances would he die.
He absolutely would not allow himself to die here, not at the hands of a clown.
Therefore, in this so-called life-or-death game, a gamble on luck, he had long prepared his cheating method.
Previously, he had secretly written three sticky notes in his room.
These three notes bore the numbers 8, 9, and 10.
They were on his person right now, always ready to be used for cheating.
Of course, this was only one of his cheating tactics.
Because earlier, when he proposed this game method—writing numbers 1 to 10 on ten paper balls—the clown suggested adding 100 more sticky notes with no numbers.
This dramatically increased the difficulty of cheating.
So, he thought the clown was pretty smart.
Thus, the pre-written 8, 9, and 10 notes were just backup plans.
He was afraid that while he wrote the numbers 1 to 10 in front of the clown, the clown, being clever, might leave a mark and write again on those 1 to 10 numbered notes.
If that happened, his previously written 8, 9, and 10 cheat notes would become useless because they wouldn’t bear the clown’s handwriting.
But the facts proved he had overestimated the clown.
The clown didn’t think of that at all.
That meant Wang Tao didn’t need to consider other cheating methods. This one alone was almost guaranteed to work.
The preparations before the life-or-death gamble were all ready.
Now, the opaque rectangular liquor box sat on the living room coffee table, exactly between the two of them.
Wang Tao said, “Do you want to draw first, or should I go first?”
“After drawing, do we open them immediately, or open them together?”
The clown said, “Whatever, I don’t care. Since it’s a life gamble, I believe in my life and my luck.”
Wang Tao replied, “Since I thought up this game, I’ll draw first. As for opening the paper balls, we open them together.”
The clown nodded in agreement.
His face wore an exaggerated smile that never faded.
Wang Tao went first.
Because the rule was best of three, but with 100 extra blank sticky notes representing zero, the probability of a tie was very high.
Therefore, the best-of-three rule was changed to winning two rounds.
For his first draw, Wang Tao didn’t use his cheating method. He wanted to see how his luck was.
So, he drew a paper ball from the box and placed it on the table.
After he drew, it was the clown’s turn.
The clown took less than three seconds before drawing a paper ball.
“Let’s open them at the same time!”
With a relaxed smile, Wang Tao opened his paper ball.
He was surprised to find his luck was quite good!
He had drawn a numbered note—the number 3.
Although 3 was relatively low among numbers 1 to 10, don’t forget there were 100 zero-value notes in the box.
So, in this setting, 3 was actually an absurdly high number.
Wang Tao felt his luck was incredible and that he might win the first round even without cheating.The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
At this moment, the clown also opened his paper ball.
Upon seeing the number on the clown’s note, Wang Tao’s whole body trembled.
His pupils dilated, and he muttered, “How is this possible? You actually drew a 4?”
That’s right, the clown drew the note with the number 4!
Excluding the number 3, there were still 109 paper balls left in the box.
Among those 109, there were only seven numbered balls: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10.
The chance of drawing one of those seven was 7 out of 109!!!
This luck was simply unbelievable!
“Looks like my luck is better than yours.”
The clown laughed loudly.
Wang Tao took the clown’s drawn paper ball and examined it carefully in his hand.
He suspected the clown had cheated.
Otherwise, how could his luck be so good, drawing a number bigger than his own?
And it was exactly one digit higher. Was fate really that coincidental?
But after looking it over, the number 4 was written in his own handwriting, which was very unique and hard to fake.
Therefore, this note was indeed written by him.
“I’m just insanely lucky,” Wang Tao thought, then his right hand touched the paper ball with the number 10 in his pocket, pressed between the pad of his thumb and flesh.
Then, his left hand threw the previously drawn 3 and 4 back into the paper box, and he let the clown shake the box to mix things up.
Originally, Wang Tao hadn’t planned to cheat so early, but the clown’s ridiculous luck had already won once. If the clown won again, he would lose.
If he lost, was he really going to hand over his life?
Wang Tao began his second draw, but this so-called second draw was just for show.
“I’ve drawn. Your turn.”
Wang Tao said to the clown.
The clown’s second draw was just as fast, and within seconds he pulled out a paper ball.
Wang Tao sneered internally and opened his own paper ball. There, glaring at him, was the number 10.
He stared at the clown’s painted face and thought, after winning this round, he would immediately use number 9 to end this boring game in the next round.
As for whether he would kill the clown after winning?
Heh.
He was already responsible for over a dozen deaths. One more wouldn’t matter.
Who told the clown to come looking for him at this late hour to play a life-or-death game?
Then let the clown leave his life here!
The clown also opened his second drawn paper ball.
Upon seeing the number 10 on the note, Wang Tao was stunned, frozen for more than ten seconds.
Then, he got so excited his face flushed red, he stood up, slammed the table so it thudded loudly, and shouted, “Impossible! Absolutely impossible!”
Wang Tao refused to believe anyone could be that lucky.
Out of 110 paper balls, he had drawn the only number 10?
What kind of god-defying luck was this?

chapters.title: Chapter 110: The Clown's Power Drill
chapters.content:
"You cheated! You definitely cheated!"
Wang Tao examined the paper ball drawn by the clown and was horrified to discover it bore his own handwriting!
Refusing to believe it, he proceeded to take out every single paper ball from the entire box.
This process took time, while the clown across from him sat on the chair, making exaggerated gestures and laughing at him.
Wang Tao's eyes were bloodshot as he took them out one by one.
Ten minutes later.
He made the terrifying discovery that the box contained no paper ball with the number 10.
This meant the clown had genuinely drawn the number 10 ball!!!
What the hell, was his luck really that good?!
"You cheated! I already drew number 10, how could you possibly have drawn it too?!"Wang Tao's mind raced quickly.
After all, he'd been a top student since childhood, attended prestigious universities, and joined major corporations.
A skilled professional, a high-level white-collar worker with considerable income.
Having a sharp mind was a given.
Especially during crises, his reaction and processing speed were exceptional.
Therefore, he decided the best defense was a good offense.
He falsely accused the clown of cheating.
The clown watched Wang Tao at this moment.
Simply repeating the motion of pointing at Wang Tao while clutching his stomach with laughter.
After this repeated several times.
The clown finally spoke: "The cheater knows who he is, hehehehe..."
"It must be you who cheated!"
Wang Tao stared into the clown's black eyes, speaking with such conviction you'd think the real cheater was opposite him.
The clown didn't continue the cheating debate, merely saying:
"I forgot to tell you one thing—our life-and-death game prohibits cheating. Anyone caught cheating must cut off one of their own hands."
"The reason I forgot to mention this anti-cheating rule is that no one's ever cheated before. Never imagined I'd encounter it today."
Wang Tao sneered: "Fine then, you cheated, so cut off your own hand!"
Wang Tao clung to one idea—never admit guilt, always accuse the opponent.
Hearing this, the clown continued laughing hysterically.
"Same as before—the cheater knows who he is. Since the cheater stubbornly refuses to admit it."
"Then the opponent must enforce the cheating penalty—hand amputation."
Having said this, the clown prepared to stand up.
Apparently ready to enforce the cheating punishment.
But in that critical moment.
Wang Tao, who had already stood up earlier, suddenly attacked.
His right hand drew a sharp dagger from his waist and stabbed toward the clown's chest.
This was the same dagger he'd grabbed when he went to the bedroom earlier for paper and pens.
A contingency plan, preparing for all possibilities.
Wang Tao's greatest life lesson was always having backup plans—without them, you'd get screwed.
Facing this ambush, the clown reacted as if expecting it, his right hand swiftly and skillfully grabbing Wang Tao's dagger-holding wrist, initiating a struggle for control.
Wang Tao hadn't anticipated the clown's reflexes and combat skills.
To directly seize his dagger-wielding hand.
Cold sweat broke on his forehead.
"But you stupid clown! Fast reactions mean nothing! Your fatal mistake was underestimating me—when I went to the bedroom for paper and pens, you didn't follow!"
During their deadlock, Wang Tao's free left hand reached to his waist again.
Producing an electric stun gun crackling with current in his left hand.
So this was Wang Tao's sneer about—besides the dagger, he had another contingency!
"Taste this!"
Wang Tao pressed the stun gun against the clown's right arm while laughing maniacally: "Come on, why not try grabbing this?! You took the dagger, let's see you take this!"
The clown's free left hand indeed didn't attempt to grab the stun gun.
First, it was difficult to seize;
second, he probably hadn't anticipated Wang Tao hiding a stun gun too.
Normally, carrying a dagger for self-defense was extreme enough.
Who prepares so many backup weapons?
Realistically, stun guns are hard to wrestle away—all components tightly packed in the handle, risking electrocution during attempts, unlike daggers.
Since seizing it was impossible, the clown should've released Wang Tao's dagger hand and retreated.
Yet inexplicably, he stood completely still.
Playing right into Wang Tao's hands.
The stun gun made direct contact with the clown's right arm.
The clown's thin clothing offered no protection.
Electric current scorched his sleeve, burning flesh beneath.
This stun gun.
Might not knock someone out instantly, but could certainly disorient them severely.
Wang Tao smirked triumphantly—but within three seconds, his smile vanished, replaced by terror.
He suddenly realized.
His stun gun seemed completely ineffective—the clown's grip on his dagger hand remained steel-strong.
Moreover, the clown's body showed zero reaction to the electricity—not even a twitch!!!
"Hehehehe"
The clown's eerie laughter instantly transported Wang Tao into the horror films about killer clowns he'd watched.
As if he'd become the protagonist.
And this clown, the terrifying antagonist.
"Look here."
The clown suddenly commanded.
In his dazed state, Wang Tao instinctively looked at the clown's mouth.
The clown abruptly opened wide, spewing forth an endless stream of snow-like white paper scraps.
Blanketing Wang Tao's face completely.
Being just paper, it caused no physical harm but completely obstructed his vision.
In this blinded moment.
The clown kicked Wang Tao's chest, sending him sprawling.
Before Wang Tao could react on the ground, countless punches rained on his face and body, forcing him to curl into a fetal position.
The kick had made him drop both dagger and stun gun.
The beating paused after three seconds.
As Wang Tao tried rising, terrifying electric paralysis shot through his waist.
His eyes widened seeing the clown smiling while electrocuting him with his own stun gun.
One shock wasn't enough—he administered a second.
Maximum voltage instantly extinguished Wang Tao's consciousness.
When he awoke, he found himself tied to a chair.
Completely immobilized.
Before him stood the clown, still in his own home.
But the situation had turned dire.
The clown now wielded a power drill.
Plugged in, its metal bit spinning at terrifying speeds.New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on
While less visually intimidating than a chainsaw.
That depended on context.
Used on human flesh...
Even a tiger would be drilled full of bloody holes!
Stress poured sweat down Wang Tao's forehead.
"What are you going to do to me?"
Wang Tao asked, nerves stretched to breaking point.

chapters.title: Chapter 111: Wang Tao, Deceased
chapters.content:
The clown laughed loudly and said, "Don't worry."
"I'm not that kind of sadistic freak who enjoys torturing people."
"You cheated in our life-and-death game, so I'll start by drilling off one of your hands with this power drill."
"Then, because you cheated and tried to kill your opponent, I hereby sentence you to death!"
As soon as the clown finished speaking, he moved with unbelievable speed. The rapidly spinning drill bit plunged directly into Wang Tao's right palm.
Instantly, the center of his palm was shredded into a bloody pulp, leaving a gaping hole.
Though Wang Tao was a deranged criminal with over a dozen murders to his name, he was still human and could feel pain.
Faced with this level of agony, he immediately began wailing and screaming in torment.
The skin on his face and exposed areas twisted grotesquely from the pain.
Veins bulged violently beneath his skin from the sheer intensity of it.But Wang Tao was still Wang Tao.
If it had been one of the lab rats undergoing this drilling torture instead,
they would undoubtedly be begging for mercy and crying for help.
He didn't. Despite being in excruciating pain,
he neither screamed for help nor begged for mercy.
Though he desperately wanted to live, he knew all hope was lost.
He had completely fallen into this clown's hands.
Even when he shocked the clown with the stun gun, there had been no reaction. He had lost fair and square.
Since the drill had only penetrated the center of his palm initially, leaving his fingers intact, the clown proceeded to drill through each of Wang Tao's five right fingers.
This elicited another round of soul-rending screams and howls of agony.
These screams should have echoed throughout Alice Apartment,
but unfortunately, Wang Tao's room—like all the psychopaths' rooms—had been specially soundproofed by the apartment management.
After just two drilling sessions, limited to his hand so far,
Wang Tao's mental state had already deteriorated drastically compared to before.
The clown then drilled Wang Tao's right hand eighteen more times.
By now, Wang Tao's right hand—still tightly bound by rope—had been reduced to a pulpy mass of flesh and blood, with even the white bones shattered into fragments.
It was a truly gruesome sight.
"Alright, next I'll drill straight into your heart,"
the clown declared with a hearty laugh.
"Heh... I should never have opened that door..."
Wang Tao mumbled weakly, his head drooping after having one hand completely destroyed.
The clown tilted his head. "It wouldn't have mattered. Even if you hadn't opened the door, I would have broken in to play this life-and-death game with you."
Wang Tao gave a cold chuckle. "Whatever... Before I die, there's one thing I want to know..."
The clown kept his head tilted, smiling. "What is it?"
Wang Tao: "Did you cheat? I refuse to believe your luck was that good..."
The clown laughed. "No, I never cheat."
Wang Tao strained to lift his head and lean it against the chair back.
Though his face still showed pain, there was now a hint of relief in his expression:
"I don't believe you. I'm about to die, and you're still lying to me."
The clown: "I truly never cheat. If you had won this life-and-death game, I would have accepted death willingly."
Wang Tao wanted to curse. If he couldn't win even by cheating, how could he possibly have won?
"Just get it over with."
Wang Tao closed his eyes.
They say your life flashes before your eyes when you're about to die.
Wang Tao was now experiencing this phenomenon.
Scenes from his entire life played like a movie in his mind.
The childhood friend he'd pushed into the river.
The college goddess and her boyfriend.
His wife, and the two children that weren't his.
The family living upstairs...
Finally, the image that lingered in his mind was that college goddess from his youth...
"Turns out... you were always the one I loved most... loved enough to kill you..."
"How frustrating... to die like this..."
Bzzzzzz.
The drill bit plunged into Wang Tao's chest, effortlessly shredding his heart...
...
Day 2, Round 27.
Mike was smoking on the rooftop of Alice Apartment.
He sipped strong coffee to stay alert.
He hadn't slept all night.
As someone accustomed to all-nighters, staying up wasn't the issue—it was the mental toll this particular night had taken.
It was now 7:00 AM.
The sun had already risen.
Mike took out his phone and dialed a number.
The line rang repeatedly with no answer.
It wasn't until the third attempt that someone finally picked up.
A groggy, half-asleep male voice came through:
"Uh... who is this?"
"It's me, Mike."
"Oh... Mike... What's up? Did you find Zhou Wu and his father?"
"Not yet. I'm calling to ask if you deposited 10,000 yuan into my bank account?"
"That... no..."
"Could it have been Zhou Yan or Li Miguo?"
"Hold on, let me check."
About fifteen minutes passed before the voice returned:
"No, they've been with me this whole time. Neither would know your account number anyway. I just confirmed with them—definitely not them."
"Why do you ask? Something wrong?"
"Oh, nothing. Maybe a friend sent it. I'll talk to you later."
Mike hung up and took a deep drag from his cigarette, squinting thoughtfully.
Yesterday, after witnessing Wu You's murder by the chainsaw killer, followed by a team of strangers cleaning up the crime scene before the police arrived,
he had been reeling from everything he'd seen.
Then, shortly after midnight—technically the next day—
he received a text notification about a 10,000 yuan deposit into his account.
The unexpected transfer had left him bewildered.
Who could have sent it?
His first thought was Jimmy and the other two who'd hired him.
He'd tried calling immediately, but there was no answer.
He then contacted other possible senders, though the chances were slim.
All confirmed they hadn't sent any money.
After more failed attempts to reach Jimmy's group, he'd resigned himself to waiting for a callback.
Of course, he never really believed Jimmy's group had sent the money.
But confirmation was necessary.
As a detective, hypothesis testing was fundamental to his work.
From the moment that 10,000 yuan appeared at midnight,
he'd been hypothesizing and analyzing.
Who sent this money?
More importantly—why?
After a whole night of intense deliberation,
and now finally confirming it wasn't from Jimmy,
he'd mostly pieced it together.
He just needed to verify a few more things to confirm his theory.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt

chapters.title: Chapter 112: The First Matchmaking Event
chapters.content:
After Sun Yijie woke up in the morning, he found the notification that money had arrived in his bank account, and he was ecstatic beyond belief!
Originally, he had signed an agreement with that person, intending to use Alice Apartment only as a refuge.
He had even prepared himself that if he got discovered here, he would just keep running!
So, he never expected to actually get 10,000 yuan per day!
But now, it was really given!
With this, he could not only take refuge but also have 10,000 yuan to spend every day—it was simply delightful.
After all, he had been living paycheck to paycheck for years, spending whatever he had.
He had been chased and hunted by that young married woman’s husband all this time, and his money was almost gone.
Now, this was just perfect as a supplement!
As for why such a big “pie” of 10,000 yuan per day and a high-end apartment fell from the sky for him?Was this pie poisoned?
Heh, so what if it was poisoned?
He even dared to mess with that married woman, so what was he afraid of?
At this moment, Sun Yijie was wearing a black tank top, his chest and back muscles bulging grotesquely.
His two arms were so thick they were even thicker than other people’s thighs.
There was a full-length mirror in his bedroom.
He kept admiring himself in it, adjusting his posture, looking at his perfect, bull-like physique.
This was the confidence that made him unafraid of any agreement, dangers, or tricks in Alice Apartment!!!
Even the boxing king Tyson would have to call him “bro” in front of him!
He thought that if he ever went to fight, one punch would teach Tyson and Ali a lesson!
People tend to become overly confident when blinded by their own confidence.
Perhaps Sun Yijie was currently stuck in such a state, but he didn’t realize it.
Of course, whether he regretted messing with that married woman or not—he definitely did regret it.
After all, he was discovered after a few times and then chased down.
“Sigh, it’s just that the other side is too powerful, with too many brothers. If it was one-on-one with her husband, I could crush him with one hand!”
After admiring and adjusting his body, Sun Yijie went to the open kitchen.
He prepared a cup of protein powder for the morning.
While making the protein powder, he played with his phone.
He was a social butterfly.
He had accounts on many social apps in the country.
He often posted his selfies and workout photos on these accounts.
Through these, he attracted the opposite sex.
As for what he did after attracting them—hehe, all men understood that.
But because he had recently been chased, he stopped posting his recent workout photos on all his social accounts.
Even though many women and some men privately messaged him, he didn’t reply.
He dared not reply.
Why?
Because all his social accounts were being monitored and even baited by that married woman’s husband.
He remembered being almost caught after being baited not long ago.
Because of this, he hadn’t been with a woman for a long time.
His mind itched, and his body itched as well.
Gulp.
After drinking a cup of prepared protein powder, he got ready to make breakfast, planning to do some simple exercise after eating to keep his figure, and then handle other matters.
And just at that moment,
he suddenly saw the residents’ group chat for Alice Apartment on WeChat.
Manager Xiao Zhang sent a message:
[At 7 PM tonight, the first-ever matchmaking event at Alice Apartment, hosted by me, officially begins!]
[The first matchmaking event will be held in the activity room on the first floor. Xiao Zhang will prepare a lavish buffet there.]
[All single men and women living in the apartment are welcome to participate! Find your match early!]
[Note: Participation in the first matchmaking event is limited to apartment residents only!!]
Looking at this message, which was sent only five minutes ago,
Sun Yijie’s eyes rolled wildly.
Suddenly, he slapped his thigh.
He was ecstatic: “God is really favoring me! I actually got to meet such a good opportunity!”
He had already searched the housing prices online yesterday.
Fifty-one thousand yuan per square meter.
A high-end apartment.
Those who could live here were either rich or had very good conditions.
If he could find a partner here, wouldn’t that be fantastic?
Both wealth and beauty!
Of course, marriage was out of the question.
But having some fun was still possible.
After all, it had been a long time since he had been with a woman.
Moreover, he was hiding in Alice Apartment, and that married woman’s husband didn’t know.
This matchmaking event was only for residents, so he wasn’t afraid that her husband would send people to bait him.
Therefore, he could safely show off his masculine charm.
“I must participate in this matchmaking event!!!”
…
The news about Manager Xiao Zhang’s matchmaking event spread throughout the entire apartment.
Of course, some were interested, and some were not.
For example, the Demoness sisters, Qin Yi and Qin Kelian, were very interested.
However, they were not interested in matchmaking but in hunting.
And those uninterested included Su Mi, the married woman living in Room 202.
She already had three little dogs in reserve and didn’t plan to add more, so she was indifferent to the matchmaking event.
At the matchmaking event tonight in Alice Apartment, aside from a few lab rats, most of the residents coming were probably like the Demoness sisters.Thɪs updatᴇd by No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
On the surface, it was matchmaking;
in reality, it was hunting.
Jiang Ran also saw this message.
He was somewhat surprised but also somewhat unsurprised.
Not surprised because he had heard from Manager Xiao Zhang before that he planned to hold a matchmaking event.
Surprised because he thought it was just talk.
He didn’t expect it to really happen, and that it would be held tonight.
Then, even more absurdly, Xiao Zhang sent him a private message.
He told Jiang Ran he had to come to the matchmaking event tonight to boost attendance, fearing that if few came, it would be awkward.
At the same time, he offered 50 yuan per hour as overtime pay for attending the matchmaking event.
At first, Jiang Ran hesitated, but after seeing the money, he decisively decided to help his good colleague!
At this time, Jiang Ran was not in Alice Apartment.
He was at the hospital entrance.
Since he last noticed the changes in his mental and physical condition, which were different from before he transmigrated,
he wanted to see a psychiatrist.
Before transmigration, his secondary personality occupied his body, but his main personality would not fall asleep and would be aware of what the secondary personality did, just unable to control the body.
After transmigration, when the secondary personality appeared, the main personality would fall asleep like other dissociative identity disorder patients, completely unaware of what the secondary personality did with the body.
He hadn’t realized this before and thought that after transmigration, the secondary personality just didn’t come out, maybe because he changed bodies or took low-quality medicine that used poison to fight poison, and that his dissociative identity disorder was improving.
But now it turned out he was wrong.
Not only was it not improving, it was getting worse!
At present, Jiang Ran had discovered that his secondary personality had come out at least twice.
He wasn’t even sure if it was the same secondary personality because he had several personalities inside him...
So now Jiang Ran was going to see a doctor.

chapters.title: Chapter 113: Psychiatric Visit
chapters.content:
Nancheng City Red Leaf Psychiatric Hospital.
This was a private specialized hospital.
Reportedly the best place for psychiatric treatment in Nancheng City.
Although the fees were relatively high here, Jiang Ran felt that going to a cheaper, low-quality hospital would be worse than staying home counting stars.
Since he had already made an online appointment, after checking in at Red Leaf Psychiatric Hospital, he began waiting for his turn with the doctor.
Jiang Ran checked the time—exactly 10:00 AM.
With several people ahead of him, he wandered around the patient waiting area.
During his stroll, he happened upon a poster.
The poster featured a doctor and his credentials—the very doctor Jiang Ran had booked an appointment with.
Named Bai Xiaoliang.A rather handsome man.
30 years old, PhD.
Had been studying in America since graduate school.
Continued through his doctorate before returning home.
Below was a long list of honors this Dr. Bai Xiaoliang had received.
All sorts of impressive achievements that dazzled the eyes.
The overall impression was simply: damn impressive!
Just then, the electronic announcement system sounded:
[Patient Jiang Ran, number 20, please proceed to examination room 1!]
[Patient Jiang Ran, number 20, please proceed to examination room 1!]
The announcement repeated three times.
Hearing it was his turn, Jiang Ran walked unhurriedly to examination room 1.
Inside, he saw the very Bai Xiaoliang from the poster—even more handsome in person.
There was a second person in the room too.
A female nurse in white sitting at a computer.
This nurse had delicate features and wore strikingly alluring red contact lenses.
"Hello, what seems to be the problem you need help with?"
Bai Xiaoliang asked across the examination desk with a smile.
So far, Jiang Ran thought Bai Xiaoliang seemed decent.
At least he could smile when facing patients.
After all, many doctors treated patients as if they owed them a million bucks, wearing gloomy expressions.
Of course, Jiang Ran understood—doctors seeing different patients all day must be exhausting.
"I have dissociative identity disorder."
Jiang Ran replied calmly.
Hearing this, Bai Xiaoliang immediately dropped his smile and turned serious.
