Round 27, Day 5, 5 AM.
The Neighbors Over Distant Relatives live stream room suddenly displayed the long-haired beautiful host on screen.
She announced the death of Sun Yijie, along with the 2.9 million wagered on him, which was all added to the final prize pool.
However, it was unclear whether it was because it was too early or because Xiao Q and Mike’s heated moments earlier that morning had caused the current online viewer count to be very low.New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
As a result, very few people were discussing Sun Yijie’s death.
So regardless of anything else, one question remained: Where was Sun Yijie’s body?
And how did he die?
Naturally, it was from being slowly executed by Lingchi Master Sherlock.
He was sliced more than 3,700 times!
(Sherlock was originally a demonic corpse, but due to some irresistible factors, the story was revised to portray him as a sadistic pervert who loved lingchi.)
After Sun Yijie died, Sherlock left room 901 and handed Sun Yijie’s battered corpse over to Xia Xiaomei for disposal.
Essentially, to handle the aftermath.
Sun Yijie should be one of the most horribly tortured deaths in the apartment’s history.
Because his torture and death lasted for such a long time.
A full entire day.
Time reached 8 AM.
Currently, there were only three lab rats left in round 27.
Jiang Ran, Wang Anjian, and Mike.
At this moment, Jiang Ran had already woken from sleep and was washing up, preparing to go to Red Leaf Psychiatric Hospital.
He had previously gone to see Dr. Bai Xiaoliang at this hospital, but had not received a response that day. They said they would reply within three days and asked him to return to the hospital.
Also, this time he wouldn’t need to pay the registration fee.
So after receiving a text notification last night and seeing the message this morning, Jiang Ran took a day off to see the doctor.
Soon it was 9 AM, and Jiang Ran arrived at Red Leaf Psychiatric Hospital.
After arriving, Jiang Ran went straight to the floor where Dr. Bai Xiaoliang had seen him before and found the nurse at the front desk, explaining who he was and why he was there.
This floor’s front desk nurse seemed to have been instructed beforehand, so upon seeing Jiang Ran, she immediately took him into Clinic Room 1.
At that moment, Clinic Room 1 was empty.
The nurse smiled and said to Jiang Ran, “Dr. Bai and the others haven’t arrived yet. Please wait here a moment.”
Then she left the room.
Jiang Ran noticed the nurse was quite young, probably two or three years younger than him.
She was rather pretty.
Feeling a bit bored in the clinic room, he started playing on his phone.
Watching videos.
About fifteen minutes later, people came into Clinic Room 1.
First was the red-contact-lens nurse from last time.
Then Bai Xiaoliang, the prodigy in psychiatry.
Jiang Ran thought it was just these two.
But it wasn’t.
Seven or eight doctors in white coats entered the clinic one after another.
Jiang Ran twitched all over, feeling like he had some terminal illness and that this was an expert consultation.
After Bai Xiaoliang came in, he said to Jiang Ran, “Jiang Ran, we have confirmed your illness. It is the diagnosis you received at the other hospital before—dissociative identity disorder.”
Last time when Bai Xiaoliang examined Jiang Ran, he couldn’t be sure whether it was dissociative identity disorder or some other mental illness.
Therefore, after Jiang Ran left the hospital, Bai had consulted with his father, the hospital director, and other doctors here.
He had also contacted some psychiatrist friends overseas via video conference.
Many psychiatric authorities were among them.
They had a heated discussion regarding Jiang Ran’s condition.

chapters.title: Chapter 136: The Second Meeting with Bai Xiaoliang
chapters.content:
Everyone had their own opinions.
Some believed Jiang Ran had dissociative identity disorder, while others thought it was not and might be another type of mental illness.
But in the end, after comprehensive consideration,
this group of people diagnosed Jiang Ran with dissociative identity disorder.
And the main person responsible for this diagnosis was Bai Xiaoliang’s teacher.
His teacher is currently one of the top three authorities in psychiatry worldwide.
An American, currently residing in the United States.
Bai Xiaoliang learned his hypnosis techniques from this teacher.
This teacher said that Jiang Ran resembled a patient he had encountered many years ago.
Both the EEG and the brain MRI scans were strikingly similar.Even the scales and questionnaires showed perfectly normal scores.
Hypnosis could not communicate with the other personalities within him.
At that time, the teacher could not be certain and even consulted two other top psychiatrists from the world’s top three authorities. The final conclusion was that it was highly likely dissociative identity disorder, requiring long-term observation.
Eventually, after prolonged observation, dissociative identity disorder was confirmed.
Therefore, this teacher began treating and controlling the patient.
Unfortunately, he ultimately failed.
Because that patient, for a period of time later, was controlled by an unknown personality within his body.
He committed many crimes and finally engaged in a gunfight with American police, where he was shot dead on the spot.
At this moment, Bai Xiaoliang sat in Consultation Room No. 1, in the doctor’s seat, while other medical staff in white coats either stood behind him or by the walls.
These people were all there to observe and learn because Jiang Ran was not an ordinary patient.
“By the way, Jiang Ran, which hospital diagnosed you with dissociative identity disorder before?”
Before deciding on a treatment plan for Jiang Ran, Bai Xiaoliang first asked which hospital had previously diagnosed him.
He was very curious about which hospital had diagnosed Jiang Ran.
After all, Bai Xiaoliang himself had put in great effort to confirm Jiang Ran’s dissociative identity disorder, even consulting a whole bunch of people including his own teacher.
Given his level of expertise, how could other hospitals have been able to confirm it? Or perhaps the hospital Jiang Ran previously visited had top psychiatrists like him?
“Uh… it was a small hospital, which no longer exists now.”
Jiang Ran felt a bit speechless inside. He had traveled through time and space after all;
he certainly couldn’t say he had been to hospitals on Earth, right?
As for traveling to this place, he indeed visited other hospitals in Nancheng City because he needed prescriptions.
But he didn’t know how that hospital in Nancheng City confirmed he had dissociative identity disorder. The process was very simple: they confirmed it and then prescribed medicine... Of course, that doctor seemed a bit careless and irresponsible. There were many bad reviews as well...
It was probably just that they heard Jiang Ran say he had dissociative identity disorder and needed medication, so they casually went through the motions and prescribed it, boosting their performance metrics.
“A small hospital?!”
Hearing this, Bai Xiaoliang was incredulous. It was so difficult to diagnose—how could a small hospital that no longer exists have confirmed it?
Or was the doctor who treated Jiang Ran back then an incompetent physician who thought Jiang Ran might have dissociative identity disorder and treated him accordingly?
Such doctors do exist.
If that was true, then it was really a stroke of luck.
At this point, Jiang Ran added, “At that time, they didn’t think the condition was so complicated. Mainly, when I went for treatment, the personalities suddenly appeared. It wasn’t like now. I was still young then, so the personalities popped out very easily.”
At this, Bai Xiaoliang suddenly understood.
And Jiang Ran wasn’t lying about this;
that was indeed a long time ago, when he was a child.
“Alright, Jiang Ran, have you recently taken any medication? Or undergone any treatment?”
Bai Xiaoliang inquired.
Jiang Ran said, “I haven’t done any targeted training or treatment for a long time.”
“As for medication, I used to take this kind, now I take this kind.”
Jiang Ran showed Bai Xiaoliang photos of the trash medicine he bought when he first arrived here, as well as two bottles of American medicine given to him by Wang Qingzhao.
Of course, the photos were saved on his phone.
Bai Xiaoliang was now holding Jiang Ran’s phone and looking at it.
Seeing the first bottle, he thought Jiang Ran must be poor;
otherwise, he wouldn’t be taking such cheap medicine with poor efficacy and side effects. But when he saw the second bottle, he went numb and froze.
He thought his eyes were deceiving him.
He rubbed his eyes in disbelief and looked multiple times to confirm he wasn’t mistaken.
Good grief, had Jiang Ran suddenly become rich?
If he wasn’t mistaken, this was the newest American medication for treating dissociative identity disorder.
It’s not even available for purchase yet in China!
It has to be bought directly from the United States!
So, what’s going on?!
First the trash medicine, now the top-tier medication?
“I’m a bit curious, how did you get this second bottle?”
Bai Xiaoliang voiced his question.
At the same time, he placed the phone on the table for other doctors to see this latest American medicine.
Jiang Ran said, “I didn’t buy it myself. A friend helped me buy it from the United States.”The source of thɪs content is NovᴇlFirenᴇt
“What’s wrong, doctor?”
Bai Xiaoliang smiled, “Nothing, this medicine is very good. You can continue taking it.”
“Next, let’s talk about other aspects!”
“Jiang Ran, last time you came, I asked if your parents or relatives had any history of mental illness.”
“You said you were an orphan, so I want to ask, did you suffer any major psychological trauma or injury during childhood?”
“In many cases, patients with dissociative identity disorder experienced brain trauma or stimuli during childhood that the brain could not accept, causing personality splits. Is that the case for you?”
Jiang Ran shook his head. “Probably not. Although my childhood was hard, I didn’t experience any trauma or injury.”
Bai Xiaoliang asked again, “Then, during your later growth or life experience, did you encounter any major upheaval or stimulus? Don’t lie to me;
I’m preparing for your subsequent treatment plan.”
Jiang Ran shook his head again. “No, nothing. Although I’m an orphan, I met many kind people while growing up. Other than lacking money, there’s nothing else.”
Bai Xiaoliang nodded. “Alright, I understand.”
“Then, recently, have you had any insomnia, hallucinations, restlessness, obsessive thoughts, irritability, a tendency to break things, difficulty communicating, or feelings of insecurity?”
“In general, patients with dissociative identity disorder usually exhibit some of these.”
Jiang Ran still shook his head. “None of those. Besides the other personalities inside me, my daily life is very normal.”
Bai Xiaoliang said nothing.
A young doctor behind him said, “Then, Jiang Ran, if everything is normal, what illness are you here for? Just keep taking your medicine regularly, right?”
Other doctors nodded as well. From their perspective, Jiang Ran’s current state was very good. The main personality’s life was normal, without any chaos. Just maintain it, and it would be fine, right?
Bai Xiaoliang motioned for them to be quiet. He believed that if Jiang Ran truly thought his life was fine, he wouldn’t be seeing a doctor. Would he not take his medicine normally?
There must be some issue.
“Jiang Ran, what problem do you want me to help you solve? Be specific.”
Bai Xiaoliang asked very seriously.

chapters.title: Chapter 137: Mike Says Goodbye to Bai Ze
chapters.content:
Jiang Ran said, “My situation is very special.”
“In the past, when the secondary personalities took over my body, my main personality—that is, myself—would not fall asleep and would clearly know what the secondary personalities did while occupying my body.”
“But now, it’s different. When they take over, I fall into a deep sleep.”
Bai Xiaoliang frowned. Just as expected, this was completely different from ordinary dissociative identity disorder patients.
After all, in typical cases, the main personality never knows what the secondary personalities do when they take control.
“Anything else?”
Bai Xiaoliang asked.
Jiang Ran nodded. “Actually, I don’t mind them coming out, but the problem is that several of the personalities inside me have huge issues. If they come out for too long, I’m afraid one day I’ll end up in jail…”
Hearing this, Bai Xiaoliang’s expression grew extremely serious.
The other doctors, however, smiled somewhat mockingly, seeming to think Jiang Ran was exaggerating or just bragging—there was no way it was that serious.Bai Xiaoliang said, “So, your other personalities are all very dangerous?”
Jiang Ran nodded. “A few are fine. If you don’t provoke them, they won’t mess with you. But some… are like those twisted serial killers, you know what I mean?”
Pfft!
Hearing this, a young doctor in the consultation room couldn’t help but laugh outright.
Bai Xiaoliang turned to ask him what was so funny.
The young doctor said, “This is ridiculous. It feels like reading a horror novel or watching a suspense movie or TV show. If your other personalities were really that twisted, you’d probably be in jail right now.”
Jiang Ran heard this and found himself unable to refute it.
Bai Xiaoliang instead glared angrily at the young doctor and told him to get out.
As a psychiatrist, how dare he question and mock his patient like that? Didn’t he know it was a huge taboo?
Don’t be fooled by Bai Xiaoliang’s handsome, warm appearance. When he scolds someone, he’s merciless.
The young doctor was immediately kicked out. The remaining doctors inside didn’t dare to make a sound, let alone laugh.
At this moment, Bai Xiaoliang regained his composure and asked Jiang Ran, “Jiang Ran, after treatment, what outcome do you hope to achieve?”
“Do you want all the other personalities to disappear and only your main personality to remain?”
“Or do you want to be able to stay awake even when the other personalities take over?”
Jiang Ran said, “Ideally, the treatment would cure everything and leave only me.”
“But I know that’s almost impossible and very difficult, so it all depends on you, doctor.”
Bai Xiaoliang exhaled deeply for a long time. “Alright, I understand. But because your case is so special, we can’t give a definite treatment plan right now. I’ll notify you next time. As compensation, there will be no registration fee next time.”
Jiang Ran nodded. “I’ll wait for your good news.”
Then he left Consultation Room 1.
After Jiang Ran left Consultation Room 1, Bai Xiaoliang turned to the seven or eight doctors beside him.
The young doctor who was kicked out earlier now stood outside the door, secretly listening to the conversation inside.
Bai Xiaoliang noticed but said nothing.
He asked the other doctors, “What do you think about Jiang Ran’s dissociative identity disorder?”
The young doctor who had first suggested Jiang Ran didn’t need to come in for treatment, only to keep taking medication normally, shared his opinion:
“Jiang Ran’s dissociative identity disorder is indeed very special. Except for the possibility that the secondary personalities might pop out, there are no other negative symptoms. Normally, his condition is very good. But if what he says about his other personalities is true, and they are very dangerous, then we must deal with those other personalities. At the very least, we cannot allow them to randomly appear.”
The others expressed similar views.
After all, Jiang Ran really didn’t seem like other dissociative identity disorder patients.
Other patients with this disorder often suffer from many psychological and physiological problems.
For example: abnormal behavior, silent personality, sensitivity, hallucinations, insomnia, anxiety, suicidal tendencies, rage, tendency to harm others, memory loss, memory confusion, identity confusion, and so on.
According to Jiang Ran, he had none of these...
Bai Xiaoliang said immediately, “Yes, Jiang Ran’s condition does seem much better than ordinary dissociative identity disorder patients.”
“But have you considered one thing?”
The other doctors looked puzzled. “What thing?”
Bai Xiaoliang’s face became grave. “Is the Jiang Ran I saw last time really the main personality?”
“And are the experiences and situations he described actually true?”
The other doctors were shocked, probably never having thought about this.
Bai Xiaoliang continued, “My American mentor, you all attended the meeting to confirm Jiang Ran’s condition. You know my mentor once had a patient very similar to Jiang Ran.”
“You also learned that many patients’ secondary personalities are born to protect the main personality, taking on what the main personality cannot bear.”
“But some are not.”
“My mentor’s patient’s secondary personalities were all insane and twisted. Forget protecting the main personality—they wanted to eliminate the main personality and take over.”
“There’s something I forgot to tell you.”
“After confirming Jiang Ran’s diagnosis, my mentor privately warned me to be cautious.”
“When he treated that patient years ago, he found that the personality he was in contact with was actually a secondary personality pretending to be the main one. Its purpose was to use my mentor’s treatment to kill the real main personality and replace it.”
“So he told me to repeatedly confirm if the personality I’m interacting with is really the main personality.”
“Never cause an accident where a secondary personality becomes the main personality.”
“That would be like opening Pandora’s box.”
After hearing this, the other doctors all gasped sharply, their expressions extremely serious and even a bit fearful.

So he returned to the apartment earlier.

At that moment, inside the management office.

Xiao Zhang said yes.

Manager Xiao Zhang directly told Mike.
Mike turned and headed straight to the place Xiao Zhang had given him.
When Mike got on the elevator, Jiang Ran had already taken the elevator up.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet

After ringing several times, the door finally opened.

“I came right in, Bai Ze,” Mike said.
Bai Ze nodded.
Then Mike walked inside, speaking as he went:
“You told me Room 1001 holds the answers I want and the secrets of this apartment.”

chapters.title: Chapter 138: Mike Leaves Alice Apartment
chapters.content:
"I want to ask, do you know whether Zhou Wu and his father are dead, or were they imprisoned like those three?"
Mike asked.
At that time, he hadn’t gotten any definite news about Zhou Wu and his father from Xiao Q and the others, so he intended to ask Bai Ze directly.
To see if Bai Ze knew.
After Bai Ze welcomed Mike inside, he poured a cup of tea for him and gestured for him to sit on the sofa. Bai Ze himself also sat down.
The white leather sofa was somewhat prone to showing dirt.
But it perfectly highlighted Bai Ze’s skin, which was even whiter than the sofa.
Bai Ze said, "I know what happened to those two."
"But tell me, do you think there’s such a thing as a free lunch in this world?"
At that moment, Mike pulled out a stack of USD from his pocket."Is this enough?"
Mike was straightforward;
if it could be solved with money, he would definitely use money.
Besides, in China, he was using the high-value USD.
That stack was probably worth five or six thousand USD, equivalent to forty or fifty thousand Chinese yuan.
But Bai Ze shook his head.
Mike thought it was because the money wasn’t enough.
So he said, "Too little? I can add more. Just name a number."
Bai Ze said, "No need for you to pay. You’ve already been compensated. You went to 1001 and rescued those three. That counts as your payment."
Mike pondered for a moment and said, "That doesn’t count. Those three also gave me very important information, which helped me decide to rescue them."
Mike pushed the money toward Bai Ze.
Bai Ze didn’t hesitate and took it directly.
Then he said, "Zhou Wu and his father are already dead."
Mike’s eyes narrowed. Although he had expected it, hearing it confirmed still shocked him slightly.Follow current novels on
He asked, "What about the bodies?"
He didn’t ask who killed them;
it was unnecessary. They were already dead, and he wasn’t going to avenge them.
Bai Ze replied, "The bodies have long been gone. The murderer who killed them disposed of the bodies. That happened many days ago."
Mike nodded. "I understand."
Mike said, "By the way, do you have any proof to back up what you’re saying? Of course, I’m not saying I don’t trust you. You should understand my situation."
Bai Ze shook his head. "No evidence."
Mike said, "Alright then, but thanks anyway."
Then he stood up and left.
Bai Ze only looked at Mike’s departing back indifferently.
Mike left Bai Ze’s home and returned to 404.
404 had been severely damaged by the chainsaw murderer.
After Mike’s confrontation with Su Mi ended, he returned here.
He discovered the tragic state of 404.
He guessed that something had happened here related to Xiao Q and the others.
But what exactly had happened, he didn’t know. Nor did he know how 404 became such a mess, so badly ruined.
At that time, Mike was clearly confronting Su Mi. Under normal circumstances, Xiao Q and the others should have been safe.
But seeing this scene, Mike immediately thought Su Mi had accomplices.
That was why she could confront him on the 10th floor for so long without being anxious.
For the same reason, he inspected the entire 404.
Looking down from the balcony window, he saw large patches of blood.
He didn’t know what happened to Xiao Q and the others.
Whether they escaped or called the police.
So, at that time, he went to the surveillance room to check the footage.
Although the surveillance was often tampered with or edited.
But this time, strangely and luckily,
The footage showed no signs of tampering or editing.
Mike successfully watched the entire process.
He saw the three arrive on the fifth floor, chased by the chainsaw murderer who had killed Wu You, all the way to 404, then descend from 404 to the first floor along a cloth rope.
Although all three were injured, in the end, they at least escaped.
Their lives were saved.
After this, it was almost morning, and Mike saw many staff come to 404 to clean up, repair what needed repairing, and replace what needed replacing.
By the time Mike returned now, 404 was brand new.
After returning to 404, Mike packed his things, apparently preparing to leave.
He packed everything into a large backpack, then carried a blue suitcase to the rooftop, folding the telescope and putting it into the suitcase.
Finally, he went all the way down to the first floor.
Upon arriving on the first floor, he happened to lock eyes with Manager Xiao Zhang sitting in the management office.
Manager Xiao Zhang smiled and walked toward him:
"Mike, what’s with this outfit?"
Mike said, "I’m leaving, leaving this apartment."
Manager Xiao Zhang was stunned, probably not expecting Mike to leave.
He asked, "Really? You’re not joking, right?"
Mike lifted the backpack on his back: "All that needed to be done, all that needed to be understood, is finished."
"Enjoy yourselves."
After speaking, Mike walked out through the automatic glass door, leaving confidently behind him.
Manager Xiao Zhang watched Mike’s departing figure, pouted his lips, and said, "With you leaving, a bunch of people will be heartbroken."
The “bunch of people” he referred to were those in the live stream room who had bet on Mike.
At this moment, anyone following Mike would never have guessed.
Mike suddenly played a bold move.
This round wasn’t over yet!
He was actually about to leave Alice Apartment!!!
So, what consequences would this cause?!
First: Mike hadn’t signed any agreement, so he could leave Alice Apartment anytime, anywhere.
Second: If he left and didn’t return before midnight tonight, even if he returned on subsequent days of this round, in the betting, he would be counted as having lost directly.
Therefore, those who bet on Mike in the live stream room were terrified, cursing nonstop.
They could accept losing their bets, and accept their lab rats getting killed.
But they absolutely could not accept losing because the lab rat left the apartment early.
Live stream room.
Ultimate Rich Kid: "Gan Lin, Mike! You foreigner! No honor! Come back quickly! Aren’t you still planning to take revenge on Robert?!"
Ultimate Rich Kid had bet one million on Mike!
And it was his first bet. He definitely didn’t want to lose on his very first bet!
Others who bet on Mike were also anxious, but anxiety didn’t help. This was the freedom of someone who hadn’t signed any contract.
Including Jiang Ran. If he suddenly left for a few days this round, it would also count as losing this round directly.
Middle-aged Uncle laughed heartily in real life, then typed: "Hahaha, well done! Mike, you should strike hard against those who bet on you, especially Diamond Bachelor! Let her use privileges to target Jiang Ran!!!!"
Those who bet on Jiang Ran had not forgotten that Diamond Bachelor used privileges to arrange for Robert to kill Jiang Ran this round.
Then she bet on Mike herself to reap the benefits.
Now, seeing Mike like this, everyone was gloating.
Ultimate Rich Kid: "What’s so funny? Maybe this round, neither Mike nor Jiang Ran will win! But that Wang Anjian who has cancer might win!"
Ultimate Rich Kid made a valid point. After all, Robert still intended to target Jiang Ran. If he succeeded in killing Jiang Ran before Wang Anjian died, then those who bet on Wang Anjian would be the final winners.
If that really happened, it would be a huge dark horse.
A super upset!

chapters.title: Chapter 139: Mike Meets with Zhou Yan, Li Miguo, and Jimmy
chapters.content:
“Heh, it’s fine. Even if Jiang Ran dies, as long as Mike doesn’t win, I’m relieved.”
The middle-aged uncle said coldly.
From this sentence, it’s not hard to see that he harbored extreme hatred toward the Diamond Bachelor.
He didn’t even care about himself anymore.
The live stream room was bustling with noise, very chaotic.
Strangely, the Diamond Bachelor, who had bet 30 million diamonds on Mike, did not say a single word in the live stream.
Indeed, she didn’t speak in the live stream.
But in reality, she was “speaking” loudly.
In the Diamond Bachelor’s princess suite, it was discovered that this young lady kept cursing nonstop and smashing things, causing the originally incredibly luxurious princess suite to almost turn into ruins.
The Diamond Bachelor was furious!She never expected Mike would leave the apartment ahead of schedule.
Although if he returned before midnight tonight and continued to stay, it wouldn’t count as a loss yet.
But the hope was really slim.
“Die! All of you, just die!”
The young lady was already on the verge of madness.
...
Did Mike really just leave like that?
Did he leave the apartment?
Was he no longer going to take revenge on Robert?
No, Robert’s grudge definitely had to be settled.
But he didn’t intend to stay in the apartment to do so.
After failing to catch Robert last time and checking the surveillance—only to find it had been tampered with—he realized that it was basically impossible to find Robert inside the apartment. Someone was deliberately blocking him.
If that’s the case, then he’d leave the apartment and avoid the labyrinth set by others.
He had already scoped out a tall hotel outside the apartment building.
He would observe the entire apartment from the hotel.
He didn’t believe he couldn’t seize an opportunity.
Besides, his initial reason for coming to Alice Apartment was to investigate Zhou Wu and Zhou Wu’s father.
Though he had neither seen them alive nor found their bodies, information about them came from Bai Ze.
Bai Ze also couldn’t provide evidence to prove whether the two were really as he claimed.
But that no longer mattered.
He didn’t want to waste time proving it anymore.
Therefore, after settling in the tall hotel opposite Alice Apartment,
he made a phone call.
Zhou Yan, Li Miguo, and Jimmy.
The four met in a private room of a restaurant.
Since returning to China, Zhou Yan, Li Miguo, and Jimmy had put complete trust in Mike, handing over all tasks of finding her father and brother to him.
The three of them were busy having wild fun elsewhere.
Today, Mike’s sudden contact gave the three a premonition—he probably found Zhou Wu and Zhou Wu’s father, so he reached out.
At this moment, there were more than a dozen delicious dishes on the table in the private room.
But none of the four present seemed to have an appetite;
not a single chopstick moved.
Zhou Yan and the others were eager to know why Mike had contacted them.
Mike, however, had no appetite because of Robert.
Zhou Yan was the first to ask, “Mike, did you find my brother? And my dad?”
Mike nodded, then shook his head.
Zhou Yan didn’t understand what Mike meant.
Li Miguo seemed to understand and asked, “You found clues but haven’t found them in person yet?”
Li Miguo thought if they had been found, there should be two more people in this private room.
Mike was straightforward and disliked beating around the bush.
His previous actions and words had shown that.
Therefore, he directly revealed the answer:
“I did investigate your dad and brother, but it’s very bad news.”
“Your dad and your brother—they’re already dead.”
“Dead?!”
After hearing this, Zhou Yan’s tone skyrocketed as she sat up in shock from her chair.
Li Miguo’s reaction was similar, though not as strong since they were not his own brother and father.
“Yes, they’re dead.”
Mike sighed.
Zhou Yan slowly sat down and after a while, asked absentmindedly, “How did they die?”
Mike: “They were killed.”
Zhou Yan’s eyes widened. “Who killed them?”
Mike said, “Someone from Alice Apartment.”
Zhou Yan: “I’m asking specifically who?!”
Mike said, “What good does knowing do? Can you take revenge?”
Zhou Yan: “I can report them to the police and have them arrested!”
Mike shook his head and then said:
“That’s useless. Reporting it to the police won’t help. From when your mom reported them missing before, you should’ve realized this isn’t that simple.”
“Zhou Yan, what I’m about to say might not be what you want to hear, but this is my advice.”
“For the brother and father you’re looking for, just accept that they’re already dead.”
“Focus on living your own life.”
“As for revenge, don’t even think about it. You don’t have that ability.”
“There’s a deep secret hidden behind that Alice Apartment. Knowing it won’t do you any good, so let’s just leave it at that.”
“Leave it at that?!”
Zhou Yan sneered, “Fine, Mike, since my brother and dad were killed, where are their bodies now? They should at least be buried properly, right?!”
Mike said, “They’ve long been gone, disposed of by the murderer.”
Zhou Yan: “Oh, in that case, do you have any evidence to prove that my brother and dad really died? That they were killed? Physical or testimonial evidence?”
Mike’s eyes turned cold. “Are you suspecting I’m lying, making up stories to deceive you?”Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
Zhou Yan sneered, “I just want proof that my brother and dad are really dead. Otherwise, I can’t believe just anyone’s word. Otherwise, I’d suspect you’re scamming my money.”
Mike remained silent for a long time.
After a while, he said, “I’m sorry. I have no evidence.”
“Of course, I’m not making up stories to deceive you.”
“It’s also because I can’t provide evidence that from the start I didn’t intend to ask you for payment. Even if you offered it, I would return it to you. As for airfare and lodging, you don’t need to pay either.”
“Our contract ends here.”
After saying this, Mike stood up and was about to leave.
Zhou Yan and the others were stunned.
Wait, why are you running away?
You don’t want the money?
“Mike!”
Jimmy chased after him.
When Jimmy and Mike left the private room,
Zhou Yan turned to her boyfriend Li Miguo and erupted angrily.
“Look at you! What kind of trash detective did you find?! Tenth best in Miguo? I think he’s the absolute worst!!!”
“He said my brother and dad are dead, but he can’t even provide proof!!!”
Li Miguo felt wronged. Actually, it wasn’t him who hired Mike but his classmate and friend Jimmy.
He could only comfort Zhou Yan.
After about ten minutes, Jimmy returned.
Upon Jimmy’s return, Zhou Yan expected him to apologize, after all, what kind of trash detective did he find?!
But Jimmy opened his mouth with:
“I just talked with Mike.”
“I’ve known Mike a long time. His character and reputation are impeccable.”
“Your brother and dad are definitely dead, even though he can’t produce evidence.”
“Before he left, he warned us.”
Zhou Yan asked irritably, “What did he say?”
Jimmy said, “If you want to stay alive, stay far away from Alice Apartment.”

chapters.title: Chapter 140: The Scheming Pretender Zhou Yan — The Joker and Jiang Ran’s Impending Clash
chapters.content:
"Trash detective! Trash detective!"
"If I'd known this American detective was so useless! I should have just hired someone from our own country!!!"
Zhou Yan's temper had always been rather explosive, queen-like in its intensity.
Right now, she was cursing openly without restraint, completely ignoring that Jimmy—the one who had brought Mike—was standing right beside her.
But Jimmy didn't seem to mind, defending Mike instead: "Mike isn't some trash detective. I think what he said is the truth."
Zhou Yan slammed the table and shouted: "I want evidence! Evidence!"
"I need to see them alive or find their bodies!!!"
Seeing his girlfriend like this, Li Miguo quickly suggested: "How about this, Xiao Yan? Let's find other detectives to investigate this matter. We'll hire several this time instead of putting all our hopes on one person. What do you think?"
This was exactly what Zhou Yan liked about Li Miguo.
When facing difficulties, he provided solutions instead of standing by helplessly.But another problem emerged.
Why had they asked Jimmy to find a detective in the first place?
The reason was simple: neither Zhou Yan nor Li Miguo had any connections in this field...
Jimmy stepped forward: "If you're still willing to trust me, I'll take responsibility for finding them."
Zhou Yan said: "Fine, but this time, don't bring me any foreigners. Find me domestic detectives only."
This woman Zhou Yan was actually quite scheming.
Did you really think her earlier anger, her furious cursing at Mike, was just because of her bad temper, because she didn't believe Mike, because she thought Mike was scamming them?!
Not entirely.
She did have somewhat of a temper.
But she wasn't an idiot.
As her father had said back in the day, Zhou Yan surpassed Zhou Wu in every aspect—it was just a pity she wasn't born male.
Regarding what Mike had said—
that her brother and father were actually already dead—
she wasn't unbelieving.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ
She actually believed it.
As for why she demanded evidence from Mike and such,
it was actually just finding fault, not wanting to pay that 1 million USD reward.
She had originally wanted to find reasons to pay less, but didn't expect the other party to be so forthright, not even wanting the money.
Since she didn't need to pay, then why after Mike left did she still pretend to curse him and act like she didn't believe her brother and father were dead?
Including later wanting to find more detectives? And only Chinese detectives?!
It still came down to that one word: money.
Earlier, pretending not to believe Mike and demanding evidence was to avoid paying that 1 million USD or reduce the amount.
After Mike left, continuing to pretend disbelief to make Li Miguo suggest finding more detectives—actually, even if Li Miguo hadn't suggested it, she would have proposed it herself.
The reason was: she believed her brother and father were dead.
So, after both of them died, how should their assets be handled?
Let's not talk about Zhou Wu—a worthless brother without much to squeeze, at most a few hundred thousand, maybe a million.
The big money was her father.
Her father hadn't left any will.
According to Chinese law,
half of her father's cash and assets would go to her mother.
Then the remaining half would be the inheritance,
to be split equally between her and her mother.
Since they had no other relatives—grandparents had all passed away—
she could get at most one-quarter of what her father left, while her mother would get three-quarters.
Now, Shen Xing was pregnant. They'd gone to a private hospital a few days ago and discovered it was a boy.
And her mother was actually quite biased toward sons over daughters.
If nothing unexpected happened, her money might all go to her grandson in the future.
So, she absolutely would not acknowledge, and absolutely would not spread news of her brother and father's death back home.
She wanted to use this time to find ways to get more of the inheritance.
As for why she later wanted to find detectives again, specifically Chinese detectives—
because Chinese detectives are paid in Chinese yuan, which is cheaper!
Unlike paying USD, where 1 USD equals 7 Chinese yuan.
Of course, finding detectives was also because, although she believed her two relatives were dead, they were still relatives.
They shared blood, there were family feelings. She couldn't be completely cold-blooded and heartless.
She still needed to find out exactly who killed them, then get revenge for her brother and father.
As for Mike's repeated warnings not to approach Alice Apartment again—
heh, if she were afraid, she wouldn't be Zhou Yan.
Who says women are inferior to men?
Even if this small apartment had something fishy, had danger—you, Mike, alone could retreat unscathed.
Why couldn't she, Zhou Yan, do the same?
...
1:00 PM.
Jiang Ran was in his home, Room 304.
He had taken two of the American pills Wang Qingzhao gave him.
Then he stayed home watching movies.
What kind of movies?
All those old films from twenty-thirty years ago, even forty-fifty years ago.
Watching these old movies, he could discover pleasant surprises.
That was, he could see some familiar actor faces—what they looked like when they were young.
Not gonna lie, they were really quite good-looking when young. Of course, some actors when young, well... were just young...
While Jiang Ran watched these old movies, he didn't quite understand why,
but inexplicably, he felt his heart could always easily calm down.
Just as he was watching a movie about a love story from decades ago,
his phone made a ticking sound.
Picking up the phone, he saw that a resident needed his help to solve a problem.
Jiang Ran had taken the whole day off today.
Just like last time when he went to see a doctor,
he had also taken a day off, only to encounter Xia Xiaomei needing his help.
Now he encountered another resident needing his help.
He deeply remembered: helping during non-work hours paid 50 yuan...
Well, he really needed money, so he chose to go.
Live stream room.
Ultimate Rich Kid: 【Hey, who lives in this 203?】
Those watching the live stream saw Jiang Ran's phone screen
and noticed a resident living in 203 needed Jiang Ran's help.
But there was no name.
Fairy Sister: 【Don't know.】
Little Aunt: 【Same here.】
Middle-aged Uncle: 【Big trouble, I know—it's that clown!】
Ultimate Rich Kid screamed: 【The clown?! Hey, right, last time that clown was waiting at Jiang Ran's place, right? But when Jiang Ran returned last time, the clown wasn't there? Why did he leave early?】
Domineering Female CEO: 【Probably got tired of waiting?】
Ultimate Rich Kid: 【So this time he's smarter—directly calling Jiang Ran to his door. Really looking forward to it—will he play a life-or-death game with Jiang Ran too? Like with Wang Tao?】
Middle-aged Uncle: 【Definitely will. After all, Jiang Ran is on his must-kill list this time! Aiya, so nervous, so nervous!】
Ultimate Rich Kid: 【Why are you nervous, Middle-aged Uncle!!! Anyway, if Jiang Ran's situation turns bad, other personalities will handle the danger! Unlike me—I bet on Mike, Mike ran away, I'm desperate! My first bet! To end like this! Damn Mike, come back quickly!!!】
Middle-aged Uncle: 【Can't help being nervous—personalities aren't omnipotent. Like your friend I am the Hero said last time: if Wang Nuli had directly smashed Jiang Ran's head, smashed it to pulp, what use would other personalities be? These psychotic serial killers are all different! That's why I'm nervous!】

chapters.title: Chapter 141: Jiang Ran: Help! I Ran Into a Psychotic Serial Killer!
chapters.content:
Jiang Ran had no idea who lived in Room 203.
But he figured he'd find out when he got there.
When he reached the door of Room 203, he noticed it was slightly ajar, not properly closed.
Just as he hesitated about whether to knock or ring the doorbell before entering,
An electronic female voice came from inside, sounding like an AI.
The voice said the door wasn't locked and told him to come straight in.
Jiang Ran pushed the door open and entered.
After stepping inside, he closed the door behind him.
His gaze was instantly drawn to something in the living room.
The living room of Room 203 was quite spacious.Aside from the basic decorative fixtures, the only other item was a television.
There was no sofa, no coffee table.
Because of this, the empty living room could accommodate very large objects.
What immediately caught his attention was a common green-felted gambling table.
Exactly like those frequently seen in movies and TV dramas.
As Jiang Ran approached and gently touched the gambling table, he suddenly realized he hadn't seen the resident of Room 203 since entering!
At that moment, a loud BANG from above his head startled him.
Jiang Ran quickly stepped back, but it was already too late.
A massive amount of colorful confetti and streamers showered down from above, covering him, the gambling table, and the nearby floor.
Wondering what it was, Jiang Ran looked closely and realized it was the kind of colorful party streamers used during birthday celebrations.
His heart still racing, he looked up and noticed a burst balloon-like object high on the ceiling - these colorful confetti and streamers had been stored inside it.
This development...
Made Jiang Ran even more confused about what kind of person lived here...
An unlocked door.
An electronic female voice.
Plus this birthday party-like situation.
While Jiang Ran was still puzzling over it, he heard PFFT PFFT PFFT sounds from a horn behind him.
Turning around, he saw a figure moving with crab-like steps, blowing a horn as it emerged sideways from the bedroom.
Only then did Jiang Ran suddenly understand.
Indeed, only that person could come up with these kinds of antics.
And that person was precisely the clown who had appeared at that welcome party!
Today the clown's outfit was identical to the one from the welcome party.
The red and white ridiculous clown costume, red ball nose, clown makeup with an exaggerated red mouth, and big red curly hair.
Now, the clown moved with comical steps over to the security door, turned around to do something unclear, then turned back and came before Jiang Ran.
PFFT PFFT PFFT went the horn.
And he said: "So, how about that preview performance?!"
Jiang Ran felt somewhat speechless, perfunctorily saying it was quite good, then immediately asked:
"Um... Mr. Clown, may I ask what you need my help with?"
Jiang Ran hadn't forgotten he came here to provide assistance.
After Jiang Ran's question, the clown stopped blowing the horn.
His posture returned to normal.
But the smile remained on his face.
He said: "I want you to play a game with me."
"A game? What kind of game?"
Jiang Ran never expected the clown wanted to play games with him?
Honor of Kings? Or PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds? Or some other game?
The clown smiled and extended four fingers.
Word by word: "A gamble-with-your-life game."
From the moment Jiang Ran encountered the clown,
The Danger Warning System in his mind had been constantly alerting:
[Ding! Dangerous person detected, please distance yourself immediately! Points +8, Points +8...]
Then, now that the clown had spoken those four words "gamble-with-your-life game,"
It directly changed to:
[Ding! Host is about to encounter danger! Please distance yourself immediately! Points +10! Points +10! Points +10...]
This was exactly like last time, when Jiang Ran, Xiao Q, and Xiao Peng's two other friends were having their door sawed through by the young white man with a chainsaw, who came in intending to kill them.
About to encounter danger, points directly maxed out at 10!
Unfortunately, last time other personalities were awakened by the system, resulting in that period of memory that Jiang Ran simply couldn't recall.
Even so.
Jiang Ran now listened to the frantic mechanical voice in his mind, his heart transitioning from calm beating to rapid pounding.
He could hear his own heartbeat clearly in the increasingly oppressive silence of the Room 203 environment.
At this moment, he forced an awkward smile:
"Gamble-with-your-life game? Is it a computer game? Or mobile game? Probably a horror game, right?!"
Jiang Ran wondered if he might have misunderstood?
Maybe it wasn't the life-or-death gamble he imagined?
The clown laughed: "Literal meaning, it's gambling with lives, gambling with both our lives."
"You win, I die. I win, you die."
Jiang Ran froze: "You're joking, right?"
The clown pulled a sharp dagger from within his clown costume, twirled it skillfully in his right hand, then suddenly stabbed it into the gambling table, the blade sinking deep into the surface.
"What do you think?"
Staring at that dagger for three seconds.
Jiang Ran's body suddenly moved.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NovᴇlFirenᴇt
Quick as a fleeing rabbit, he reached the door of Room 203.
He tried to open the door to escape, but to his horror discovered it wouldn't open.
The clown stood in the living room, emitting his shrill clown voice: "La la la, don't bother trying. Didn't you see I went to the door first before coming to you? Today, in this place, only one person will walk out."
Alright, alright.
Jiang Ran regretted coming here today for that 50 yuan.
But thinking carefully, if you escape the first day, you won't escape the fifteenth.
If this clown had set his sights on him, this day would have come eventually.
But, this is so bizarre!
Jiang Ran still found it hard to believe that someone in his apartment building wanted to play some kind of gamble-with-your-life game with him.
How could this be so much like a movie or novel plot? He wasn't acting in a movie!!!
"Wait, you're a clown - is everything today just rehearsal for a future performance you can't reveal to me? For realism?! When everything's over, you'll say it was all just a joke?!"
Jiang Ran still refused to give up.
He felt this must be some new type of performance, a horror thriller show.
But the clown, seemingly wanting Jiang Ran to accept reality so it wouldn't affect their upcoming gamble-with-your-life game,
Said: "Go online and search for 'clown killings' in our country, then you'll know whether this is performance rehearsal or not."
Jiang Ran pulled out his phone, originally intending to send a text to call the police during the search. Regardless of whether the clown was joking.
But unfortunately, the clown came over and stood beside him, watching closely.
Searching for "Hua Country clown killings" on his phone.
Jiang Ran prayed inwardly, hoping he wouldn't find anything.
That this was just some new performance show requiring rehearsal.
But sadly, he found results.
After finding them, Jiang Ran briefly scanned through.
It said this clown was a deranged serial killer who had murdered many people. Reading this far, he didn't continue - there was no need.
Then, he compared the clown photo from his search results with the person before him.
You couldn't say they were identical - you had to say they were absolutely the same person.
Even though both faces wore clown makeup.
The facial features and bone structure were there.
You could still clearly distinguish them.
And the clown makeup was exactly the same...
At this point, Jiang Ran deflated, collapsing to sit down heavily.
Good grief, his luck was truly terrible!
How could he have encountered a deranged serial killer?!

chapters.title: Chapter 142: The Joker’s Great Epiphany About Life
chapters.content:
At this moment, the clown patted Jiang Ran's shoulder.
"Don't lose heart, as long as you win against me in the gamble-with-your-life game, won't that solve everything?"
After speaking.
The clown had already taken his seat at the gambling table, in the dealer's position.
Jiang Ran knew there was no escaping today and could only play along.
He then sat down in the gambler's seat opposite.
But it was clear that he was quite agitated.
He said: "How do we play this gamble-with-your-life game? Let me state upfront - I don't gamble, never have gambled, don't really know how to play cards, just know how to play Fight the Landlord."
"Hehe"
The clown was amused by Jiang Ran's blunt honesty.He said: "Don't worry, the gamble-with-your-life game is very simple, very fair."
Jiang Ran asked: "What you said earlier about the winner living - is that true? If I win against you, you won't go back on your word and kill me, will you?"Follow current novels on ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
The clown shook his head: "I keep my promises."
Jiang Ran asked again: "What if it's a draw?"
The clown shook his head: "There won't be a draw. If it's a draw, we both get to live."
The clown then thought of Wang Tao, who had asked him the same question last time.
Unfortunately, that guy cheated and got killed by him.
Jiang Ran swallowed hard: "Alright, then tell me how this gamble-with-your-life game works!"
Jiang Ran took a deep breath - now he could only win this so-called gamble-with-your-life game before making other plans!
He hoped heaven would bless him and let him win!
The clown said: "Comparing card sizes with playing cards, best of three rounds, each drawing one card."
Jiang Ran thought for a moment and shook his head: "No, I've seen plenty of TV shows, movies, and novels about gambling tables. Things like playing cards, dice, and mahjong are all about cheaters versus cheaters."
"You're a clown, so you're definitely better than an ordinary person like me at things like playing cards. I don't think this is fair."
The clown was stunned. He hadn't expected Jiang Ran before him to be so similar to Wang Tao from last time.
He suddenly smiled: "In that case, I guess dice won't work either."
"How about this - last time someone suggested blind drawing from paper balls when playing the gamble-with-your-life game with me. How's that? Fair enough?"
"Last time? You've played the gamble-with-your-life game with someone else before? What happened to that person last time?"
Jiang Ran quickly asked.
The clown said: "He died, died from cheating. So I'm warning you - don't cheat. Cheating gets you a hand chopped off. Last time he both cheated and tried to kill me."
Jiang Ran said: "Then let's forget about the paper ball drawing too. The last person didn't survive, it's bad luck. Let's change the game."
The clown said: "Why don't you suggest one yourself."
Jiang Ran: "I need some time."
Jiang Ran sat there pondering hard.
The clown remained calm, smiling all the while.
At the same time, his hands kept performing various flashy tricks, especially with several colorful balls that he manipulated with utterly mesmerizing skill.
While playing, the clown suddenly asked:
"Jiang Ran, do you believe in fate?"
Hearing this, Jiang Ran temporarily stopped thinking about game options and replied: "I don't know, I've never thought about such questions. Since you're asking me, do you believe in it?"
The clown didn't answer whether he believed or not.
He said: "My life has had its peak, and after the peak came the valley. According to my thinking, after the valley should come either a return to the peak or lingering in the valley forever - that's just how life is."
"But what I never expected was that after the valley of my life came another, lower valley, and after that even lower valley came yet another, even lower valley."
The peak the clown referred to was his clown performance career at its height with high income. The first valley was when he got injured during performance, and after recovery his income drastically dropped, his clown performance career plummeting.
The second valley was when his female apprentice and wife ran away.
The third valley was falling in love with a male apprentice, only to be given by that male apprentice to others to play with.
At this point, the clown continued:
"After falling into successive valleys, I found a quite famous fortune teller."
"I asked him to tell my fortune. I only had him tell my fortune without sharing my experiences with him."
"Then he did his calculations for me, and after finishing, he said my fate was bad - though my life had its peak, what followed were all valleys with no chance of recovery."
"I asked him if there was any solution?"
"He told me that a person's entire life is designed from birth, everything is predestined. He only tells fortunes, he doesn't change fates. If he could change fates, he wouldn't be making a living telling fortunes for others here."
"At that time I thought about it, and what he said about life being designed from the start and everything being predestined - that made a lot of sense."
"For example, after my lowest valley, I wanted to make money, lots of money, but couldn't."
"I wanted to find a woman again, get married and have children, but no matter how hard I tried, I remained alone."
"I suddenly understood something."
"Yes, that saying is so true - what's meant to be will come, what's not meant to be cannot be forced."
"I cannot control my own fate. No matter how hard I try, the things I want to obtain remain out of reach."
"But! I suddenly discovered that I can control other people's fates!!!"
At this moment, despite the heavy clown makeup on his face, nothing could conceal the bizarre great enlightenment showing on the clown's face.
"I can decide the life-and-death fates of others!"
"For example, if I meet someone on the street, if I don't want to kill them, they can continue living well for now. But if I want to kill them, they're definitely dead!"
"Since I can't control myself, then I'll control others!!!!"
Jiang Ran felt a headache coming on after hearing this: "So now you want to control my fate?"
The clown laughed uproariously: "Nonsense! Aren't I gambling with your life right now? If you win against me, won't you get to live well?"
"Alright, come on, have you thought of a game yet?"
Jiang Ran shook his head.
He had thought of many options but felt none would work.
At this moment, the clown pulled open a drawer from a cabinet beside the gambling table and surprisingly took out a silver-white revolver from inside.
Besides that, there was also one bullet.
Seeing this, Jiang Ran's eyes instantly widened.
If this were free America, Jiang Ran definitely wouldn't be so shocked!
But this is Hua Country!
How do you have a gun?!
Though shocked and curious, Jiang Ran didn't ask where the gun came from.
Because that question was meaningless.
The clown now said: "Using this to gamble with lives, just like in those movies."
"This revolver can hold six bullets. Right now, I'll load one bullet into this gun. Then we'll take turns, each firing one shot. How about that?"
"If everyone's fate is predetermined from birth, then so is life and death."
"When to be born, when to die."
"If you're destined to die today, then no matter what you do, you won't survive."
After speaking, the clown placed the revolver and that single bullet in front of Jiang Ran.
"Once you've considered this game, inspect the gun and bullet. Don't think that just because I provided them, I would tamper with anything."

chapters.title: Chapter 143: Come on! You Cheat, I Cheat, Everybody Cheats
chapters.content:
Staring at the revolver and that single bullet on the gambling table.
Jiang Ran suddenly had an idea.
What if he loaded the bullet now and shot the clown—problem solved.
But then the issue popped up: he didn't know how to load a bullet, and it seemed like he had to disengage some safety to fire?
Another problem: since the clown had the gun and bullet casually tossed in front of him, he probably anticipated this exact thought. There must be countermeasures.
"Fine, let's go with this."
Jiang Ran decided to leave everything to fate!
He had no choice!The most update n0vels are published on ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
So he began to examine the revolver and the bullet.
It was his first time touching a real gun;
it looked about like what he’d seen on TV.Once he picked it up, he found it much heavier than he had expected.
For now, he couldn't find any visible problem with the gun or bullet—though more importantly, if there were hidden issues he wouldn't be able to tell.
Soon after, the revolver and bullet were pushed back to the clown.
The clown took the revolver and bullet and, with practiced ease, loaded the bullet.
He pushed out the cylinder, placed the bullet in, then pushed the cylinder back in.
Then he frantically flicked the cylinder with his finger so it was impossible to tell exactly where the bullet was.
He handed the revolver to Jiang Ran and motioned for him to flick the cylinder with his finger the same way.
Jiang Ran complied.
While doing so, he watched closely and indeed could not tell which chamber the bullet now occupied.
"Do you want to go first, or should I?"
The clown laughed loudly now;
the laugh seemed deliberately timed to press on Jiang Ran's nerves.
"You go first," Jiang Ran said.
In general, Jiang Ran was an "ordinary person." For a game like this, he preferred the other side go first—after all, this wasn't a contest where whoever took the initiative held the advantage.
The clown took the revolver from Jiang Ran’s hands, made a gesture indicating the cylinder was properly fixed to allow firing.
Then he pulled the safety off.
That meant pulling the trigger would fire the bullet.
The clown gripped the revolver in his right hand and pointed the muzzle at the temple on his right side.
He seemed utterly unafraid of death, eyes wide, face crazed, and with the red clown makeup his expression was particularly terrifying.
Then he pressed the trigger against his temple.
Click.
Only the sound of the cylinder rotating.
There was no imagined loud gunshot—meaning the clown had, by luck, survived.
Having survived, the clown immediately tossed the gun back in front of Jiang Ran.
Jiang Ran’s earlier thought returned.
Now that the gun could fire, should he take it and blast the clown a few times?
There were six rounds;
sooner or later he could hit the clown.
But a new worry emerged: what if the bullet was a blank? That would be weird.
Maybe it really was a blank.
But he couldn't be sure.
In the end, he abandoned that thought.
His right arm trembled;
his whole body was shaking for no apparent reason.
His heart hammered wildly.
Jiang Ran stared at the revolver on the table for a long time before finally picking it up with his right hand and—just like the clown—aiming the muzzle at his own temple.
At that moment he didn't know what his mind was thinking.
His eyes shut tight, teeth clenched, and he squeezed the trigger with all his strength.
Click.
No violent gunshot—meaning Jiang Ran, too, had lucked out and survived.
A relieved smile involuntarily crossed Jiang Ran’s face.
He tossed the gun back to the clown.
A wave of lightness washed through him.
He touched his forehead and discovered it was covered in sweat—so much that one hand felt sticky.
The clown didn’t take the revolver;
instead he applauded Jiang Ran.
"Good, good, good. Brave. I thought you might fire several shots at me and finish me off, but you didn't."
Jiang Ran smiled helplessly: "I was afraid it was a blank."
The clown laughed: "You guessed right. It really is a blank."
Hearing the clown admit it, Jiang Ran felt fully relaxed.
But the clown's next words shoved Jiang Ran back toward the brink.
"Don't think a blank won't kill. Compared to live rounds, blanks do have less force, but firing at the temple can still either kill or leave you gravely injured. There was an actor abroad who joked around with blanks used on set;
the unlucky first shot hit his temple. He was rushed to the hospital and fought for six days—he didn't make it."
The clown then, without another word, took the revolver from the table, pointed it at his temple, and pulled the trigger again.
After firing this shot, the clown laughed wildly and pushed the revolver back to Jiang Ran.
Just like that, Jiang Ran's brief relaxation vanished and he returned to his previous awkward state.
After all, it was his turn again.
He gripped the edge of the gambling table tightly with both hands, eyes fixed on the revolver as his thoughts frantically spun.
He didn't understand why the clown kept pointing the gun at his own temple so casually.
Was he truly unafraid of death?
Or did he already know where the bullet was?
But how could that be possible?
There are no impossibilities in this world.
To Jiang Ran, the gun was a silver-white revolver.
But through the clown’s eyes, the gun glowed blue with faint red light.
The clown was wearing a pair of special contact lenses.
They were specially treated contact lenses.
Earlier, someone had applied a kind of solution to the revolver and the bullet.
This solution had no smell and left no visible trace.
It couldn't be seen with the naked eye, but when you wore those special contact lenses you could see the residue.
That was how the clown knew the bullet's exact position.
Current situation:
The cylinder holds six chambers.
Starting from the first shot:
Numbered: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
Each time the trigger is pulled, the cylinder rotates to the right one chamber.
So far, shots one, two, and three have been fired, confirming those chambers were empty.
Therefore the bullet had to be in one of the remaining 4, 5, 6.
And unlucky for Jiang Ran, the bullet happened to be in the fourth chamber—the very chamber Jiang Ran was about to fire at his own temple.
"Looks like fate has decided you'll die here today."
The clown thought, already waiting for Jiang Ran's death.
Of course, according to his plan, a blank probably wouldn’t kill Jiang Ran outright.
No worries—he would help Jiang Ran end it all, with a power drill. He’d drill through your heart to free you.
Just like Wang Tao back then.
Now Jiang Ran shakily aimed the muzzle at his temple.
He was prepared.
He closed his eyes and, as if it was the first time, tensed his whole body.
His index finger rested on the trigger, ready to squeeze at any moment.
Just as he was about to pull it—
A cold mechanical electronic voice appeared in his mind:
[ Ding. Detected host is about to face a lethal crisis. Consume 100 points. The bullet has been moved to the next chamber. ]
The system's meaning was simple: the bullet had been in position four, and it had now shifted to position five.

chapters.title: Chapter 144: What If It Keeps Ending in a Tie? Joker: Just Break the Game Rules
chapters.content:
This happened right before Jiang Ran pulled the trigger. Hearing the system's voice,
Jiang Ran immediately pulled the trigger with tears welling up in his eyes.
A click sounded.
Jiang Ran had successfully survived.
He excitedly pushed the revolver toward the clown.
His tears could no longer be held back.
He shouted inwardly: "System, it turns out I've been wrong about you all along, I've failed you!"
Jiang Ran was saved.
His face was full of excitement, the ecstasy of surviving a near-death experience.
But the clown on the other side had his brows tightly furrowed, the previous laughter on his face completely gone.At this moment, his gaze was fixed dead on the revolver before him.
Was he hallucinating just now??ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
He saw clearly - the bullet glowing red was in chamber number 4, so how did it suddenly become number 5?
Did Jiang Ran cheat?
But how did he cheat?
The technique was completely undetectable! Not a single trace left!
The clown didn't have time to think about this problem now, because the issue he currently faced was:
The shot he was about to fire at his own temple had a bullet in it.
Especially since he knew this fact.
Even though he knew, he still quickly picked up the revolver and fired a shot at his own temple.
This shot also produced only a click sound.
When the clown put down the gun, in his field of vision,
The bullet that was previously in chamber number 5 was now in number 6.
What was going on?
It turned out the clown's revolver was very special.
The trigger was adjustable.
Depending on the angle and force of the pull, it could make the bullet in the cylinder slide to either the left or right chamber.
Then, the clown pushed the revolver toward Jiang Ran.
He wanted to see clearly whether he had been seeing things or if the other party had cheated.
At this moment, Jiang Ran was somewhat confused.
Because according to what the system just said, his bullet consumed 100 points and transferred to the next chamber.
So, the shot the clown just fired should have definitely killed him!
But it didn't.
So in this situation, two possibilities:
First: The clown cheated, though he didn't know how.
Second: The system lied, but this... honestly, in the past he would have thought the system was lying.
But now sitting across from him was a deranged serial killer who could be looked up online.
This definitely wasn't a lie...
"There are six chambers total, now it's the last one. If we remove the possibility of system point consumption and the clown cheating, then the first five had no bullets, this one definitely has one."
Now it was Jiang Ran's turn. His right hand tightly gripped the revolver, the muzzle aimed at his right temple.
Because the system was there, he wasn't too nervous.
So he took a breath, opened his eyes, stared at the clown across from him, and noticed the clown had been staring unblinkingly at the revolver in his hand.
Jiang Ran prepared to pull the trigger.
Right before pulling the trigger, the system appeared again.
[Ding, detected host is about to face a lethal crisis, consumed 100 points, bullet has been transferred to next chamber.]
He pulled the trigger. Click.
But now sitting across from him was a deranged serial killer who could be looked up online.
But now that Jiang Ran was safe, he didn't feel relieved.
Because as mentioned earlier, the revolver had six chambers total, with the bullet in one of them.
Six shots made one round. Under normal circumstances, either Jiang Ran or the clown should have been shot in the temple during this round.
Yet, one round passed.
Both of them were fine.
This was very awkward...
"Let's continue!"
The clown acted as if there was no problem with the previous round, taking the revolver from Jiang Ran's hand.
He again aimed at his own temple and fired a shot.
This shot was safe.
Next it was Jiang Ran's turn. Jiang Ran again heard the system's point consumption notification.
This shot, Jiang Ran was also safe.
The two of them continued like this, firing shots through another round.
The atmosphere at the scene became increasingly silent, increasingly oppressive.
Neither of them spoke at the moment.
Before starting a new round, the clown directly took the revolver, opened the cylinder, and clearly saw the bullet inside - a blank round.
Then he placed the revolver on the gambling table, making eye contact with Jiang Ran.
Both of them were in an extremely awkward situation.
First, Jiang Ran thought the clown had cheated.
But he didn't know how the clown cheated.
Empty accusations without proof.
And he was afraid that if he accused the clown of cheating, the clown might become desperate and directly attack him.
Then there was the clown on the other side.
He was also certain Jiang Ran had cheated.
But like Jiang Ran, he couldn't figure out how Jiang Ran cheated.
Because Jiang Ran only placed his hand on the trigger without moving at all.
Yet the bullet instantly transferred from this chamber to immediately appear in the next chamber. Like magic.
It wasn't like his method of pulling the trigger at different angles to make the bullet naturally slide from the original chamber to another one.
So, what to do now?
Should he directly stand up and say Jiang Ran cheated?!
Like with Wang Tao last time?
But with Wang Tao last time, he actually figured out Wang Tao's cheating method.
Wang Tao's cheating technique was too clumsy, after all he wasn't professional.
But this time, he could confirm Jiang Ran cheated.
But if he stood up and said "you cheated,"
And Jiang Ran responded with: "Show me the evidence, how did I cheat?" What would he do?
Because he couldn't figure out the cheating method. Didn't know how to reproduce it.
Thus, a deranged serial killer was stuck here.
So, he thought there was another problem now.
Shouldn't Jiang Ran across from him have also figured out that he cheated?
But probably like him, didn't know his cheating method.
No evidence.
After all, in this gamble-with-your-life game, the cylinder had already gone through two rounds, yet in both rounds, both of them surprisingly remained unharmed.
Frankly speaking, both of them had problems.
......
These deranged serial killers all have their own murder preferences, rules.
Or specific targets for killing, unique killing methods, etc.
Therefore, they're quite similar to certain rule-based or horror genre novels.
The ghosts and other things that appear in them all have their own unique murder rules and patterns.
If you don't trigger them, you're fine - these supernatural beings strictly adhere to them.
But humans are different;
there's an essential difference between humans and ghosts.
Humans aren't beings that will strictly adhere to their murder preference rules.
Please remember, these deranged serial killers are all human, with their own unique thoughts and thinking.
And humans differ from each other.
Some deranged serial killers indeed strictly adhere to their rules;
if they do something that doesn't conform, they feel imperfect and uncomfortable.
But some can make exceptions.
Like the current clown.
He recalled when he murdered that female apprentice wife who emptied his house and took all his money.
Then recalled that male apprentice who loved him and was also murdered by him.
Thus, a deranged serial killer was stuck here.
He just directly killed them for revenge.
Wait!
Speaking of which, why did he now enjoy playing gamble-with-your-life games with people he was about to kill?
It seemed he greatly enjoyed this process?
Watching these people's various emotional reactions before death?
Yes, that was exactly it.
What gamble-with-your-life game.
Whoever wins gets to live?
This was just a colossal lie.
He simply enjoyed controlling and toying with the life-and-death fate of the other party.
These deranged serial killers all have their own murder preferences and rules.
No matter who was the final winner in the gamble-with-your-life game, the one who died would definitely be the other party.
Not himself.
Since the gamble-with-your-life game had now reached an endless stalemate.
Might as well be straightforward - stop playing and directly take action.

chapters.title: Chapter 145: Persona Reemerges
chapters.content:
At this moment, Jiang Ran noticed the clown sitting in the dealer position at the gambling table suddenly stood up.
Jiang Ran remained highly vigilant, keeping his eyes tightly locked on him, fearing he might pull some trick.
The clown smiled: "Don't be nervous, I'm just a bit thirsty and going to get some water."
After standing up, just as expected, the clown left the gambling table, continuing under Jiang Ran's watchful gaze.
He went to the open kitchen.
Squatted down for no more than ten seconds.
When he stood up again, his left hand held a 600ml bottle of mineral water.
His right hand carried a bag of disposable paper cups.
Returning to the dealer position at the gambling table.
The clown took out two paper cups, placing one each in front of himself and Jiang Ran.Then, he opened that bottle of mineral water, preparing to first fill his own cup, then fill Jiang Ran's.
Jiang Ran watched closely, noticing the clown didn't seem to be pulling any tricks.
That mineral water bottle was also unopened, he could see clearly.
Of course, even if the other side wasn't pulling tricks, he still wouldn't drink water poured by the clown.
After finishing pouring water for himself, the clown proceeded to pour water into the paper cup before Jiang Ran.
When the bottle mouth hovered above Jiang Ran's paper cup, the clown's right hand gripping the water bottle suddenly exerted force.
Immediately, the water that should have fallen into the paper cup instead sprayed entirely onto Jiang Ran's body.
Splashed by the water, Jiang Ran instinctively stood up and retreated, and at that moment, the clown's left hand suddenly produced a black object, thrusting directly toward Jiang Ran's chest.
Turns out pouring water was just a diversion—the real purpose was to splash water on Jiang Ran to distract him, making it easier to strike.
This thrust came extremely fast.
By the time Jiang Ran noticed, it was already too late to dodge, so he could only block with his right hand.
But the moment he blocked in front of his chest, he immediately regretted it.
The intense pain transmitted through his right hand was unbearable.
So painful, so numb—the instant that thing struck his hand, he felt his entire hand and arm become useless, trembling wildly and losing control.
Only then did Jiang Ran realize—what the clown held wasn't a fruit knife, but a stun gun.
After hitting Jiang Ran's right hand, the stun gun didn't stop but continued discharging electricity.
This resulted in Jiang Ran collapsing to the ground within seconds.
His whole body convulsed and trembled.
Fortunately, Jiang Ran's eyes remained open.
Radiating intense hatred and unwillingness, his mouth mumbled incoherently:
"You're so despicable! Actually breaking the game rules! Attacking suddenly!"
The clown stepped over the gambling table, coming to Jiang Ran's side. Seeing Jiang Ran's eyes still open as if saying something, though he couldn't make it out.
Anyway, it didn't matter—he immediately gave Jiang Ran another sustained shock to the abdomen.
This time, Jiang Ran even closed his eyes, completely losing consciousness.
"Really works well, this Wang Tao's stun gun."
Examining the black stun gun in his hand—exactly the one confiscated from Wang Tao.
Finding the stun gun interesting, the clown delivered several more shocks to the already unconscious Jiang Ran, making his body jerk repeatedly.
Confirming Jiang Ran was truly completely unconscious, the clown stood up and headed toward the bedroom to prepare the next step.
The next step was simple too—tying Jiang Ran to a chair.
Then waiting for him to wake up before ending his life with the power drill.
The clown went into the bedroom to fetch tools.
Poor guy, just like the kite killer Wang Nuli back then, unaware of what's about to come.
[Ding! Detected host suffering electric shock damage, consuming 500 points! Repairing!]
[Ding! Detected host facing life-threatening danger, consuming 1000 points! Awakening other personalities!]
[Ding! Personality has been awakened!]
At this moment, the system's cold mechanical voice emerged.
And after the system's mechanical voice faded.
Jiang Ran, who had been lying unconscious on the ground, suddenly snapped his eyes open.
After opening them, he supported himself against the wall, slowly standing up.
Once upright, he stretched his limbs, then surveyed the surroundings.
After finishing his survey, he sat back down in the gambler's position at the gambling table where the main personality Jiang Ran had previously sat.
The current Jiang Ran appeared cold and detached, not a trace of smile on his face.
After taking his seat, his right hand grasped the paper cup filled with water from the clown's position opposite him.
Bringing it over, he drained it in one gulp.
After drinking, he placed the paper cup on the gambling table, then pressed his right thumb and middle finger together, taking aim before flicking the paper cup on the table with fierce force.
This flick carried tremendous power, sending the paper cup flying all the way to the balcony floor with a loud thud.
Witnessing this scene, Jiang Ran turned his head, muttering in a voice only he could hear:
"This post-transmigration body is far inferior to my Earth body."
At this very moment, the clown with a broad grin on his face had been fetching rope and the power drill in the bedroom when suddenly his ears perked up, his whole body freezing in place.
Abandoning the rope and power drill, he tightly gripped the stun gun he'd just placed on the bedroom bed and walked out of the bedroom.
Exiting the bedroom, he saw Jiang Ran sitting by the living room gambling table, looking toward him.
Seeing the clown emerge, Jiang Ran said coldly: "Quite sharp ears. Originally just wanted to test you with the paper cup, never expected you'd actually hear it."
The clown noticed one of the two paper cups was missing from the gambling table. Searching around, he spotted it on the tiled floor by the balcony.
He rarely frowned.
Wondering—was this stun gun too weak? Or was Jiang Ran's electrical resistance too strong? Waking up so quickly?
Whatever, no matter—since he's already awake, dwelling on this is pointless.
Now.
"You clown, you have no principles in how you conduct yourself or affairs. We agreed on a gamble-with-your-life game—whoever loses gives their life. The gamble-with-your-life game hasn't ended yet, and you already resort to dirty tricks."
Jiang Ran's icy gaze seemed to drop the surrounding temperature by several degrees.
The clown resumed his broad smile: "That's because you cheated."
The clown used cheating as an excuse—after all, he'd already broken the game;
whether he could detect Jiang Ran's cheating methods didn't matter anymore.
Jiang Ran sneered: "And you didn't cheat?"
The clown laughed broadly: "No, I didn't cheat."
That's right—there was one more point: the clown believed from start to finish that he hadn't cheated.
Because his behavior constituted cheating at cards.
You might ask—isn't cheating at cards just cheating?
Who said? Cheating is two characters;
cheating at cards is three characters.
The clown was simply playing word games—I cheated at cards, not cheated.
Same with Wang Tao last time.
From beginning to end, he claimed he didn't cheat.
Because he was cheating at cards.
"Say whatever you want, I can't be bothered to waste words with you."
Jiang Ran now stood up, stretching his muscles and bones, apparently preparing to take action, with no intention of continuing to argue with the clown. Ready to directly finish off this clown.
Seeing this, the stun gun in the clown's right hand continuously emitted sizzling blue electric sparks, seeming quite confident about the upcoming fight.
After properly stretching, Jiang Ran stepped closer to the clown.
When about a meter away, the clown also moved.
His movements were swift and fierce, his right hand impossibly fast, the stun gun heading straight for Jiang Ran's heart position.
This attacking motion was countless times faster than when he attacked the main personality Jiang Ran last time.
But despite being countless times faster.
When the stun gun was still ten centimeters from Jiang Ran's heart, the clown's wrist was firmly clamped by Jiang Ran's left hand.
No matter how much force the clown exerted, his right hand couldn't break free from Jiang Ran's left grip.
"Too slow, too weak."
"If you were one of those horror movie ghost clowns, I'd definitely be helpless against you—after all, you wouldn't be human."
"Unfortunately, you're not one of those ghost clowns—you're just a person."
